## Strong fits (IC, direct skill overlap)

**1. Sr. Platform Eng., Batch & Notifications** — *Engineering*
Builds scalable mission-critical batch/notification platforms with Java + Spring Boot + Kafka. **Direct analog to your Valkey+Asynq + Go pipelines on Raven.** Stack is JVM not Go, but the problem domain (durable jobs, fan-out, notifications) is exactly what you've been building.
[Apply](https://ebay.wd5.myworkdayjobs.REDACTED)

**2. Software Engineer, ML Systems** — *Engineering*
LLMs, big data, recommendation systems at scale. You're already running a Python gRPC AI worker with pgvector+BM25 RAG — same retrieval/embedding stack, just at eBay scale. Strongest "AI infra" overlap of the lot.
[Apply](https://ebay.wd5.myworkdayjobs.REDACTED)

**3. Sr Platform Engineer, Java Fmwk (Forklift)** — *Engineering*
Site-facing REST + GraphQL platform, automation, secure/scalable. Maps to your Gin API and SuperTokens/auth-SPI work — transferable, but you'd be back on Java.
[Apply](https://ebay.wd5.myworkdayjobs.REDACTED)

## Stretch fits (manager track)

If you want to step into leadership (building Raven solo suggests architect/lead mindset):

- **Software Development Manager, Platforms** — Cloud-native developer platforms (K8s, Tekton). Strong cultural fit with Raven's platform-builder ethos.
- **Cloud Traffic Engineering Manager** — Private cloud infra leadership.
- **Engineering Manager (Cloud Infra)** — Similar profile.

## Skip

Manager, Data Science & Analytics (marketing analytics); Audit and SOX Associate Manager; Manager, IT Audit — all outside your stack.

## My pick

**Software Engineer, ML Systems** is the cleanest match — your AI-worker work translates 1:1, and it keeps you on the IC track building the kind of system you're already wiring up in Raven. **Sr. Platform Eng., Batch & Notifications** is the safe second choice if you'd rather lean into pure backend platform work.

> AGENT

Read the JDs. Here's the honest take for **10 YoE**:

## The catch — all 3 IC roles are under-leveled

| Role | YoE required | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **ML Systems** | MS+3 or BS+5 | You're 2× over the bar |
| **Batch & Notifications** | 3+ yrs | You're 3× over — Senior IC band |
| **Java Forklift (Raptor.io)** | 3-5 yrs | You're 2-3× over — DevX/CI-CD level |

All three carry "Senior" titles but the YoE bands and JD scope read like **Senior/SE3, not Staff**. At 10 YoE you'd likely be underleveled & underpaid, and the work (CI/CD pipelines, Spring Boot patching, vulnerability scans, K8s upgrades) is execution-heavy, not architectural.

## Stack-fit reality check

- **ML Systems** — closest "spiritual" match (GenAI/LLM/RAG/embeddings — same problem space as your Python AI worker), but they explicitly want **Scala/Java + Hadoop/Spark**. Your stack is Python gRPC + pgvector + BM25. You'd be selling adjacency, not direct match.
- **Batch & Notifications** — conceptually = your Valkey+Asynq work, but execution stack is **Java/Spring/Kafka/Airflow**. You'd be writing JVM code daily.
- **Java Forklift** — purely Java DevX. Furthest from your Raven work (Go API, edge deployment, auth SPIs).

## My revised recommendation

```
## Existing ADRs about chunking embedding strategy

### Raven > Language > Marketplace
### Marketplace

**Marketplace**:
The cross-tenant discovery surface that lists Public KBs available for Import. Hosted at `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace`. Accessible only to authenticated Users; no anonymous browsing.

**Content-grade Publish**:
The data boundary applied when a KB is Published or Imported. Chunks, Embeddings, and Source metadata cross the boundary; original file blobs, runtime artefacts (api_keys, chats, routing_rules, webhooks, response_cache, connectors), and any non-allow-listed `settings` keys do not. See [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-content-grade-publish-boundary.md).

**Public KB**:
A KB whose publishing Org has flipped its `visibility` to `public`, making it discoverable on the Marketplace. The KB itself still lives in its publishing Workspace; visibility is the only thing that changes.

**Private KB**:
A KB visible only inside its owning Org. The default state for every KB.

**Publish**:
The act of flipping a KB from `private` to `public`. Reversible (the publisher can unpublish), but unpublish does not affect already-Imported copies. The publisher of record is the **Org**, not the User who pressed the button. See [ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-org-as-marketplace-publisher.md).

**Org slug**:
A globally-unique, URL-safe identifier for an Org. Forms the first segment of every Marketplace URL: `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace/{org_slug}/{kb_slug}`. Backfilled from `display_name` at migration; subsequently editable but constrained for uniqueness.

**Marketplace URL**:
The canonical public address of a Public KB: `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace/{org_slug}/{kb_slug}`. 404s if either slug is unknown or the target is private.

**Import**:
The act of an Org cloning a Public KB into one of its own Workspaces. Produces an independent KB row with its own Sources, Chunks, and Embeddings — a fork, not a live link. See [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-marketplace-fork-on-import.md).

**Re-import**:
A destructive overwrite of an existing Imported KB with the publisher's current state. Replaces the Importer's local Chunks and Embeddings; preserves the Importer's KB id, Chats, Widgets, and other runtime artefacts (these FK to the Imported KB id, not its content). Always confirmed.

**`last_modified_at`**:
Timestamp on a Public KB reflecting the most recent content-affecting change in the publisher's workspace. Shown as "Updated 3 days ago" on Marketplace listings; the Marketplace and Import operations both read live KB state per [ADR-0003](docs/adr/0003-always-fresh-publish-lifecycle.md) — there is no separate publication snapshot in MVP.

**`imported_from_revision_at`**:
Timestamp stamped on the Importer's local KB at the moment of Import, recording the publisher's `last_modified_at` value captured. Lets the Importer reason about what they have vs what's now available upstream.

**Importer Org**:
An Org that has Imported one or more Public KBs. Distinct from the **Publishing Org** that owns the original.

### 0001 — Marketplace KBs use fork-on-import > Consequences
## Consequences

- `knowledge_bases` gains a `visibility ENUM('private','public')` column and a `source_public_kb_id UUID NULL` lineage pointer.
- Marketplace listing is a single `SECURITY DEFINER` function returning public-KB metadata (`id`, `org_id`, `name`, `description`, counts) across all Orgs. No cross-tenant read of Chunks or Embeddings is ever needed at query time.
- Unpublish is non-destructive to Importers. The original KB flips back to `private`; existing forks continue to work.
- Quota accounting must treat Imported KBs as owned by the Importer Org (they consume Importer storage and embedding budget), not by the Publisher.

### Raven > Language
## Language

**Organization** (Org):
The top-level tenant. Owns billing, subscription, members, and all data created beneath it. Identified by `org_id` in RLS and throughout the codebase.
_Avoid_: Account, tenant, customer.

**Workspace**:
A sub-grouping inside an Org that owns one or more Knowledge Bases. Used to scope membership, API keys, and (eventually) per-team plan limits.
_Avoid_: Project, team.

**Knowledge Base** (KB):
A collection of Sources, Documents, Chunks, and their Embeddings against which Chats and Widgets are run. Belongs to exactly one Workspace.
_Avoid_: Corpus, dataset, library.

**Source**:
An input to a KB — uploaded file, URL, connector. Materializes into one or more Documents on processing.

**Chunk**:
The atomic embeddable unit of text extracted from a Document. Sized by the chunker to fit the embedding model's token window.

**Embedding**:
A vector for a Chunk produced by an embedding model. Currently `vector(768)` from `nomic-embed-text`.

**Subscription**:
The billing relationship between an Org and a paid plan. One active subscription per Org. The **Free Plan** is the implicit state when no active paid subscription exists.

**Free Plan Org**:
An Org without an active paid Subscription. The phrase "free user" is shorthand for "a User belonging to a Free Plan Org" — the plan is a property of the Org, never the User. Free Plan Orgs are governed by the strict-flywheel rule in [ADR-0004](docs/adr/0004-free-tier-public-only-rule.md): every KB they hold — whether created or imported — is forced `visibility=public`.
_Avoid_: Free user, free account (when used to imply a per-user concept).

**Read-only-private KB**:
A KB in the transitional state produced when a Paid Plan Org downgrades to Free Plan. Stays private but cannot accept new Sources, Documents, or Chats until the User Publishes it, Deletes it, or upgrades back. Represented by `kb_status = 'read_only_private'`.

**Derivative Public KB**:
A Public KB whose `source_public_kb_id` points at another Public KB — i.e. an Imported KB that was itself made public (either because the Importer chose to publish their fork, or because the Importer is a Free Plan Org and the strict-flywheel rule forced publication). Lineage is preserved indefinitely; takedowns of the original do not cascade.

### 0004 — Free Plan Orgs hold only Public KBs > Trade-offs accepted
## Trade-offs accepted

- **Derivative Public KBs create attribution tangle.** Acme Corp publishes → 200 Free Plan users import → 200 derivative Public KBs exist. Each is a separate row, each independently editable. UI must show lineage clearly (`source_public_kb_id` already on the row from ADR-0002). Solved in attribution design, not here.
- **Takedown does not cascade.** Acme retracts → derivatives still exist. Standard OSS-attribution practice: the publisher's act of making something public is irrevocable for downstream users. Mitigated by mandatory licence declaration (separate decision) which gives downstream Orgs a legal basis to keep their forks.
- **`read_only_private` is a new KB status that touches every read path.** Chat sessions must check it and surface a graceful "frozen" message; widgets must return a maintenance response; the worker must skip embedding new docs into it. Real implementation cost, but bounded — the status check piggybacks on the existing `status` column on `knowledge_bases`.
- **No grace period on downgrade.** A Paid Org that cancels lands instantly in the frozen state; their dashboards stop letting them add to private KBs immediately. We've decided friction > silent privacy decisions. A future grace-period feature can be additive.

// The first section (before or including the first heading) captures any preamble
// and the # title. Each subsequent ## heading starts a new section.
//
// Sections are then passed through capChunkBySize so any single section larger
// than maxChunkRuneCount is broken into multiple smaller chunks on paragraph
// boundaries. Without this guard, a doc with a single huge body (typical of
// PDF text extraction and long-form markdown without ## headings) becomes one
// >75 KB chunk that the embedding model rejects with "input length exceeds
// the context length" — nomic-embed-text in particular caps at ~8K tokens.
func SplitMarkdownByHeadings(content string) []MarkdownSection {
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")

	var sections []MarkdownSection
	var currentHeading string
	var currentLines []string

	for _, line := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "## ") {
			// Flush the current section if we have accumulated content.
			if len(currentLines) > 0 || currentHeading != "" {
				sections = append(sections, MarkdownSection{
					Heading: currentHeading,
					Content: strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(currentLines, "\n")),
				})
			}

…rrentHeading != "" {
		sections = append(sections, MarkdownSection{
			Heading: currentHeading,
			Content: strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(currentLines, "\n")),
		})
	}

	return capSectionSize(sections, maxChunkRuneCount, chunkOverlapRuneCount)
}

// Token-budget guard for the embedding step. nomic-embed-text caps at
// ~8K tokens. The rune→token ratio varies hard by content:
//   - clean English markdown: ~4 runes/token
//   - PDF-extracted text:     ~2 runes/token  (broken hyphenation,
//                              odd whitespace, OCR-like artefacts)
// Sizing for the worse case keeps the PDF path working too. 6000 runes
// → ~3K tokens for PDFs, ~1.5K tokens for clean markdown — comfortable
// margin under the 8K cap and still big enough that typical sections
// stay in one chunk.
//
// chunkOverlapRuneCount preserves a sliding window of context across

// splitByParagraphsWithCap walks paragraphs (separated by blank lines)
// and accumulates them into chunks of <= maxRunes runes. A paragraph
// that on its own exceeds maxRunes is hard-cut on rune boundaries with
// `overlap` runes of repetition between adjacent cuts.
func splitByParagraphsWithCap(text string, maxRunes, overlap int) []string {
	paragraphs := strings.Split(text, "\n\n")
	var chunks []string
	var current strings.Builder

	flush := func() {
		if current.Len() == 0 {
			return
		}
		chunks = append(chunks, strings.TrimSpace(current.String()))
		current.Reset()
	}

	for _, p := range paragraphs {
		p = strings.TrimRight(p, "\n")
		if p == "" {
			continue
		}
		pRunes := []rune(p)
		if len(pRunes) > maxRunes {
			// Flush whatever we'd accumulated before tackling the monster.
			flush()
			for i := 0; i < len(pRunes); {
				end := i + maxRunes
				if end > len(pRunes) {
					end = len(pRunes)
				}
				chunks = append(chunks, string(pRunes[i:end]))
				if end == len(pRunes) {
					break
				}
				// Slide forward, leaving `overlap` runes of repeat for
				// continuity. Guarantees forward progress when overlap
				// >= maxRunes by clamping below.
				step := maxRunes - overlap
				if step <= 0 {
					step = maxRunes / 2
					if step <= 0 {
						step = 1
					}
				}
				i += step
			}
			continue
		}
		// Would adding this paragraph blow the cap? Flush first.
		candidate := current.Len() + len("\n\n") + len(p)
		if candidate > maxRunes && current.Len() > 0 {
			flush()
		}
		if current.Len() > 0 {
			current.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		current.WriteString(p)
	}
	flush()
	return chunks
}

		err = db.WithOrgID(ctx, pool, p.OrgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
			for i, section := range sections {
				if strings.TrimSpace(section.Content) == "" {
					continue
				}
				tokenCount := len(strings.Fields(section.Content))
				chunk := &model.Chunk{
					OrgID:           p.OrgID,
					KnowledgeBaseID: p.KnowledgeBaseID,
					DocumentID:      &p.DocumentID,
					Content:         section.Content,
					ChunkIndex:      i,
					TokenCount:      &tokenCount,
					ChunkType:       model.ChunkTypeText,
					Metadata:        map[string]any{},
				}
				if section.Heading != "" {
					chunk.Heading = &section.Heading
				}
				created, err := chunkRepo.CreateChunk(ctx, tx, chunk)
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("create chunk %d: %w", i, err)
				}

				// Best-effort embed. A retrieval-empty document is still
				// useful via BM25, so we don't fail the whole job when
				// the embedding backend hiccups — log and move on. The
				// embedding gRPC call is per-chunk; with markdown-by-
				// heading splits the chunk count is small (< 50 for any
				// realistic doc) so the latency cost is bounded.
				if embed != nil {
					vec, dims, modelName, embedErr := embed(ctx, p.OrgID, created.Content, "")
					if embedErr != nil {
						logger.Warn("chunk embedding failed; falling back to BM25-only retrieval",
							"document_id", p.DocumentID,
							"chunk_index", created.ChunkIndex,
							"error", embedErr,
						)
					} else if len(vec) > 0 {
						emb := &model.Embedding{
							OrgID:      p.OrgID,
							ChunkID:    created.ID,
							Embedding:  pgvector.NewVector(vec),
							ModelName:  modelName,
							Dimensions: dims,
						}
						if _, err := chunkRepo.CreateEmbedding(ctx, tx, emb); err != nil {
							logger.Warn("persist embedding failed; chunk indexed without vector",
								"document_id", p.DocumentID,
								"chunk_index", created.ChunkIndex,
								"error", err,
							)
						}
					}
				}
			}

			// Update document status to ready within the same transaction.
			return docRepo.UpdateStatus(ctx, tx, p.OrgID, p.DocumentID, model.ProcessingStatusReady, "")
		})
		if err != nil {
			setFailed(ctx, pool, p.OrgID, p.DocumentID, docRepo, logger, err)
			return fmt.Errorf("insert chunks: %w", err)
		}

		logger.Info("document processed",
			"document_id", p.DocumentID,
			"chunks", len(sections),
		)

		// Fire `document.processed` webhook (best-effort; never blocks the success path).
		dispatchAsync(ctx, webhookDispatcher, logger, p.OrgID,
			string(model.WebhookEventDocumentProcessed),
			map[string]any{
				"document_id":       p.DocumentID,
				"knowledge_base_id": p.KnowledgeBaseID,
				"status":            string(model.ProcessingStatusReady),
				"chunk_count":       len(sections),
			})

		return nil

// SplitMarkdownByHeadings splits markdown content into sections based on ## headings.
// The first section (before or including the first heading) captures any preamble
// and the # title. Each subsequent ## heading starts a new section.
//
// Sections are then passed through capChunkBySize so any single section larger
// than maxChunkRuneCount is broken into multiple smaller chunks on paragraph
// boundaries. Without this guard, a doc with a single huge body (typical of
// PDF text extraction and long-form markdown without ## headings) becomes one
// >75 KB chunk that the embedding model rejects with "input length exceeds
// the context length" — nomic-embed-text in particular caps at ~8K tokens.

// → ~3K tokens for PDFs, ~1.5K tokens for clean markdown — comfortable
// margin under the 8K cap and still big enough that typical sections
// stay in one chunk.
//
// chunkOverlapRuneCount preserves a sliding window of context across
// split boundaries so the next chunk doesn't start mid-thought.
const (
	maxChunkRuneCount     = 6000
	chunkOverlapRuneCount = 400

// Insert all chunks and update status in a single RLS transaction.
		err = db.WithOrgID(ctx, pool, p.OrgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
			for i, section := range sections {
				if strings.TrimSpace(section.Content) == "" {
					continue
				}
				tokenCount := len(strings.Fields(section.Content))
				chunk := &model.Chunk{
					OrgID:           p.OrgID,
					KnowledgeBaseID: p.KnowledgeBaseID,
					DocumentID:      &p.DocumentID,
					Content:         section.Content,
					ChunkIndex:      i,
					TokenCount:      &tokenCount,
					ChunkType:       model.ChunkTypeText,
					Metadata:        map[string]any{},
				}
				if section.Heading != "" {
					chunk.Heading = &section.Heading
				}
				created, err := chunkRepo.CreateChunk(ctx, tx, chunk)
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("create chunk %d: %w", i, err)
				}

				// Best-effort embed. A retrieval-empty document is still
				// useful via BM25, so we don't fail the whole job when
				// the embedding backend hiccups — log and move on. The
				// embedding gRPC call is per-chunk; with markdown-by-
				// heading splits the chunk count is small (< 50 for any
				// realistic doc) so the latency cost is bounded.
				if embed != nil {
					vec, dims, modelName, embedErr := embed(ctx, p.OrgID, created.Content, "")
					if embedErr != nil {
						logger.Warn("chunk embedding failed; falling back to BM25-only retrieval",
							"document_id", p.DocumentID,
							"chunk_index", created.ChunkIndex,
							"error", embedErr,
						)
					} else if len(vec) > 0 {
						emb := &model.Embedding{
							OrgID:      p.OrgID,
							ChunkID:    created.ID,
							Embedding:  pgvector.NewVector(vec),
							ModelName:  modelName,
							Dimensions: dims,
						}
						if _, err := chunkRepo.CreateEmbedding(ctx, tx, emb); err != nil {
							logger.Warn("persist embedding failed; chunk indexed without vector",
								"document_id", p.DocumentID,
								"chunk_index", created.ChunkIndex,
								"error", err,
							)
						}
					}
				}
			}

			// Update document status to ready within the same transaction.
			return docRepo.UpdateStatus(ctx, tx, p.OrgID, p.DocumentID, model.ProcessingStatusReady, "")
		})
		if err != nil {
			setFailed(ctx, pool, p.OrgID, p.DocumentID, docRepo, logger, err)
			return fmt.Errorf("insert chunks: %w", err)
		}

		logger.Info("document processed",
			"document_id", p.DocumentID,
			"chunks", len(sections),
		)

		// Fire `document.processed` webhook (best-effort; never blocks the success path).
		dispatchAsync(ctx, webhookDispatcher, logger, p.OrgID,
			string(model.WebhookEventDocumentProcessed),
			map[string]any{
				"document_id":       p.DocumentID,
				"knowledge_base_id": p.KnowledgeBaseID,
				"status":            string(model.ProcessingStatusReady),
				"chunk_count":       len(sections),
			})

		return nil
	}
}

// Token-budget guard for the embedding step. nomic-embed-text caps at
// ~8K tokens. The rune→token ratio varies hard by content:
//   - clean English markdown: ~4 runes/token

//                              odd whitespace, OCR-like artefacts)
```

Looking at `internal/jobs/document_process.go` right now:

```go
const (
    maxChunkRuneCount     = 6000
    chunkOverlapRuneCount = 400

```

And `SplitMarkdownByHeadings` already calls `capSectionSize(sections, maxChunkRuneCount, chunkOverlapRuneCount)`, which in turn calls `splitByParagraphsWithCap` — paragraph-boundary splits, with overlap, exactly as the handoff describes. Comments even cite the original failure mode (`"input length exceeds the context length" — nomic-embed-text in particular caps at ~8K tokens`).

A couple of nuances I want to flag before grilling continues:

1. **Unit mismatch in the plan vs. code.** The handoff talks in *tokens* (≥6000 token cap, ~200 token overlap). The code caps in *runes* (6000 runes, 400 overlap). The comment converts: 6000 runes ≈ 3K tokens for PDF text, ≈ 1.5K for clean markdown — i.e. the code is *more conservative* than the handoff plan. Worth confirming this is intentional and not a misunderstanding when the constants were chosen.
2. **CONTEXT.md already has `Chunk` defined**: *"The atomic embeddable unit of text extracted from a Document. Sized by the chunker to fit the embedding model's token window."* No glossary collision — good.

```
## ModelPickerStep onboarding component for provider selection

### ModelPickerStep.vue (2)
<ul class="space-y-2 mb-6">
      <li
        v-for="m in visibleModels"
        :key="m.name"
        class="rounded-lg border p-3 cursor-pointer transition-colors"
        :class="
          m.name === selectedModel
            ? 'border-amber-500 bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-900/10'
            : 'border-neutral-300 dark:border-neutral-700'
        "
      >
        <label class="flex items-start gap-3 cursor-pointer">
          <input
            type="radio"
            :value="m.name"
            v-model="selectedModel"
            class="mt-1"
          />
          <div>
            <div class="font-semibold text-neutral-900 dark:text-white">
              {{ m.name }}
              <span class="text-xs text-neutral-500 font-normal">
                · {{ m.sizeGb.toFixed(1) }} GB
              </span>
            </div>
            <div class="text-sm text-neutral-500">{{ m.description }}</div>
          </div>
        </label>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <p
      data-test="selected-model"
      class="text-sm text-neutral-500 mb-3"
    >
      Selected: <code class="font-mono">{{ selectedModel }}</code>
    </p>

    <button
      data-test="pull-button"
      :disabled="pullState === 'pulling'"
      class="w-full bg-amber-500 hover:bg-amber-600 disabled:opacity-50 text-white font-semibold py-3 rounded-lg transition-colors mb-3"
      @click="pullSelected"
    >
      {{
        pullState === 'pulling'
          ? `Downloading… ${percent}%`
          : pullState === 'done'
            ? 'Downloaded'
            : 'Download model'
      }}
    </button>

    <progress
      v-if="pullState === 'pulling'"
      :value="percent"
      max="100"
      class="w-full h-2 mb-3"
    />

    <div
      v-if="errorMessage"
      class="text-red-500 text-sm mb-3"
    >
      {{ errorMessage }}
      <button class="underline ml-2" @click="pullSelected">Retry</button>
    </div>

    <button
      data-test="skip-model"
      class="text-sm text-neutral-500 underline"
      @click="emit('skip')"
    >
      Skip — I'll add a BYOK key instead
    </button>
  </div>
</template>
```

```
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, onMounted, onUnmounted } from 'vue'
import { useAuthStore } from '../stores/auth'

const authStore = useAuthStore()
const menuOpen = ref(false)

function onEscape(e: KeyboardEvent) {
  if (e.key === 'Escape' && menuOpen.value) menuOpen.value = false
}
onMounted(() => window.addEventListener('keydown', onEscape))
onUnmounted(() => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onEscape))

function handleLogout() {
  menuOpen.value = false
  authStore.logout()
}
</script>

### LlmProviderListPage.vue (2)
function onProviderTypeChange() {
  const help = providerHelp[form.value.provider]
  // Apply provider-specific Base URL default (Ollama → localhost:11434);
  // null for cloud providers that don't need it; empty string for custom
  // so the input is shown but unset.
  if (help.defaultBaseUrl !== undefined) {
    form.value.base_url = help.defaultBaseUrl
  } else if (form.value.provider === 'custom') {
    form.value.base_url = ''
  } else {
    form.value.base_url = null
  }
  // Reset the per-provider model selection to the first model in the
  // list, so the previously-selected (and possibly unrelated) model
  // doesn't leak when switching providers.
  const models = modelsForType(form.value.provider)
  selectedModel.value = models[0]?.value
  // Ollama doesn't require an API key — clear any stale value the user
  // typed before switching providers.
  if (!help.requiresKey) {
    form.value.api_key = ''
  }
}

const createError = ref('')

async function handleCreate() {
  creating.value = true
  createError.value = ''
```

## Q1 — Default semantics: is "default" single, or split by purpose?

Today the schema has a single `is_default=true` provider per org. Chat, embeddings, and RAG all resolve through this one default. The handoff history showed pain around this — your earlier fix `fix(chat): resolve org's default LLM provider instead of hardcoding 'anthropic'` made the chat call honor it, and there's a recurring bug shape ("No active 'X' provider config" / chat model leaks into embed path).

That sets up the real choice:

**(a) Keep single org-wide default.** One row is `is_default=true`. Chat and embeddings both route through it. The same provider config holds *both* the chat model (e.g. `llama3.1:8b`) and the embedding model (e.g. `nomic-embed-text`) inside its `config` JSON — caller picks which model at request time. Switching default = switching the whole provider in one click.

**(b) Split by purpose: a chat-default and an embed-default.** Two `is_default_*` flags (or a `default_for` enum). Lets you, e.g., chat with Anthropic but embed with local Ollama. More flexibility, more invariants to enforce, more UI surface.

**(c) Per-user override.** Each User picks their preferred provider for their own session; org default is the fallback.

**My recommendation: (a) — keep single org-wide default.** Reasons:
- Schema and code today already assume it. (b) and (c) are migrations + cross-cutting refactor.
- The chat-vs-embed-leak bug isn't about *which provider* — it's about *which model within a provider*. The fix lives in the model-picker, not in splitting defaults.
- Demo box has been working on (a) once `9c4e0d58` landed. Don't pile new invariants on a stack that just stabilized.
- (c) breaks the mental model that "the Org owns its config" (see CONTEXT.md's Organization definition).

If we ever need (b), we can add it as a second flag without breaking (a) consumers.

**Pick (a), (b), or (c)?**

> DEVELOPER

a

> AGENT

## Q2 — Switch action: instant or confirmed?

User clicks "Make default" on a provider that isn't currently the default. What should happen?

**(a) Instant toggle, optimistic update.** Click → UI flips the default badge immediately, fires `PUT /default` in background, rolls back with a toast on failure. No confirm dialog. Like Gmail's "default account" toggle.

**(b) Click → confirm dialog.** "Switch default to OpenAI? All new chats and embeddings will route through this provider." User confirms, then we PUT.

**(c) Confirm only when risky.** Instant for "safe" cases; confirm only when the target has `status != active` or last-tested-status is `fail`. (Risk-tiered UX.)

Two important secondary facts that constrain this:
- The default change is **global to the Org** — every other user's next chat suddenly hits a different vendor. That's not user-local; it's a tenant-wide change.
- Existing chats already in flight aren't affected (each request resolves the default at call time). So it's not catastrophic, but it *is* observable to teammates.

**My recommendation: (a) — instant toggle.** Reasons:
- The action is cheap, reversible (click another provider to undo), and the radio-style mental model is well-known.
- Existing in-flight requests aren't affected — no "data loss" risk that a confirm dialog would protect against.
- The page already has confirm dialogs for **Delete** (irreversible) and **Test Connection** (gate before Create). Adding a third confirm step would dilute the signal of the first two.
- For the "risky" case (default → an untested or failing provider), a **warn-but-allow** banner inside the card is enough — no modal.

The one cost of (a): an org admin could accidentally fat-finger a wrong provider. Mitigation = clear visual feedback (badge moves with a small transition), toast that says "Switched default to OpenAI", and the previous default is now one click away.

**Pick (a), (b), or (c)?**

> DEVELOPER

A

> AGENT

## Q3 — Edit-in-place: which fields are editable, and where do they live?

Today the page only supports **Create** and **Delete** — no Update path at all, even though the backend already exposes `PUT /llm-providers/:id`. The redesign is the first chance to add this.

Field inventory on a provider:

| Field | Editable? (gut check) | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` (openai / anthropic / ollama / custom) | No — changing this is effectively a new provider | n/a |
| `display_name` | Yes | low — pure label |
| `base_url` | Yes (Ollama tunnel rotates often) | medium — wrong value breaks chat silently |
| `api_key` | Yes (rotation) | high — write-only secret |
| `config.model` | Yes | medium — wrong model = error from vendor |
| `is_default` | Yes (via Q2) | medium — org-wide effect |
| `status`, `api_key_hint`, `created_at` | No — derived/read-only | n/a |

Three layouts to choose from:

**(a) Pure inline.** Every editable field is click-to-edit directly on the card. `display_name` becomes an input on click, model becomes a dropdown always visible, API key has an inline "rotate" button that swaps to an input. Each field saves on blur.

**(b) Pure modal.** Click "Edit" on the card → opens a dialog identical to Create, pre-filled. All edits batched, one Save button at the bottom. Same Test-Connection gate as Create.

**(c) Hybrid.** Low-sensitivity fields (`display_name`, `model`, `is_default`) inline directly on the card. High-sensitivity fields (`base_url`, `api_key`) behind a single "Edit credentials" button that opens a focused dialog — and that dialog **re-runs Test Connection** before saving (same gate Create uses).

**My recommendation: (c) — hybrid.** Reasons:
- You said "edit-in-place" — (c) honors that spirit for the fields that benefit (rename a provider, swap model in one click) without losing the safety net for the fields that *should* gate on a successful probe.
- Test Connection is a hard-won feature (commit `22cf88c6`) that exists because users were saving broken creds. An inline `api_key` edit that bypasses it would walk that back.
- `base_url` rotation (Ollama tunnels) is a common real workflow — putting it in the same dialog as `api_key` is fine because both are credential-shaped and both want a Test-Connection re-probe.
- Implementation cost is lower than (a): we already have the dialog from Create; we just open it pre-filled in "edit" mode. Pure (a) means writing per-field save flows + per-field error states.

The one cost of (c): two distinct save flows on one card (inline saves vs. dialog save). Mitigation = the inline fields autosave on blur and show a small "Saved" tick; the dialog has its own Save button. Different verbs for different stakes.

**Pick (a), (b), or (c)?**

> DEVELOPER

c

> AGENT

## Q4 — API key edit semantics in the Edit dialog

The dialog from Q3(c) handles `base_url` + `api_key`. The `api_key` is encrypted at rest, never returned by the API, and only its prefix is exposed via `api_key_hint`. So the dialog can't pre-fill it. The question is how the field *behaves*.

**(a) Masked-pretend placeholder.** Show `sk-•••••0a4f` as a faux value in the field. Typing replaces; empty = preserve. Pro: clear what's there. Con: looks editable but isn't — users will hit backspace and not know if they cleared the real key or just the placeholder.

**(b) Empty input + helper.** Field always starts blank with helper text "Leave blank to keep existing key". Submit-blank = preserve. Submit-value = replace. Pro: explicit. Con: cognitive load on every save; common case (rename, swap model) shows an unwanted password field for no reason.

**(c) Explicit "Rotate key" affordance.** Field is **hidden by default**. A small `Rotate API key` button (or disclosure) reveals an empty input. Submit replaces. Skipping the button = key untouched. Pro: zero ambiguity, no secret-shaped UI noise until you ask for it. Con: one extra click when you *do* want to rotate.

Two backend implications you should know before answering:

1. **Test Connection currently requires `api_key` in the request body.** If the user edits the dialog without rotating, the probe has no key to send. Either (i) the backend's `POST /llm-providers/test` learns to take `{provider_id}` and use the stored key, or (ii) the frontend skips the probe when neither `api_key` nor `base_url` changed. (i) is the cleaner long-term move; (ii) is a one-line client guard. We'll need one or the other regardless of which UX we pick here — but (c) makes the decision more obvious, since "no rotate" → "no key in form" → trivially route to (i) or (ii).
2. **`api_key_hint` is already shown on the card** ("API key configured" / "not set"). The edit dialog doesn't need to repeat it as a placeholder.

**My recommendation: (c) — explicit "Rotate API key" affordance.** Reasons:
- Matches the mental model of secret rotation (write-only, never displayed).
- Removes the "is that the real key or a placeholder?" footgun in (a).
- Removes the wasted password-field-in-every-edit noise of (b) — most edits won't touch the key.
- Makes the Test-Connection backend choice easy: dialog opens with no key in state; only carries one if Rotate was clicked. If no rotate → call probe with `provider_id` only.
- Keyless providers (Ollama) just don't render the Rotate button — same `requiresKey` flag already used on the Create form.

The cost: one extra click for the rotate path. Acceptable.

**Pick (a), (b), or (c)?**

```json
  "file_path": "/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-llm-provider-management-design.md",
  "content": "# M13 — LLM Provider Management UI\n\n**Status:** Draft (review pending)\n**Date:** 2026-06-02\n**Milestone:** M13 — AI Provider Management UI\n\n## Problem\n\nToday the `/llm-providers` route lets a user **Create** and **Delete** providers but offers no way to:\n\n- **Switch** the default provider between existing rows. The backend has `PUT /llm-providers/:id/default` and the store wraps it, but the list page only auto-defaults on the *first* create. A user with two providers cannot flip between them without deleting one.\n- **Edit** existing providers. Rotating an API key, fixing a stale Ollama tunnel URL, or renaming a provider all require delete-and-recreate today.\n- **See the current default at a glance.** The card layout does not surface `is_default`.\n- **Reach the page from the user-profile menu.** `AppHeader.vue` dropdown contains only \"Sign out\". Discovery today is via Settings → button or the mobile tab bar.\n\n## Goals\n\n1. Make the default provider switchable from the list page with one click and an obvious visual indicator.\n2. Allow editing of existing providers in-place where safe, in a dialog where credentials are involved.\n3. Wire entry points so the page is reachable from the user-profile dropdown (and the desktop sidebar).\n4. Preserve every existing safety net: Test Connection gate, write-only API keys, encrypted-at-rest storage, RLS scoping.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- Per-purpose default split (chat-default vs embed-default). See ADR-0006. Single default per Org stays.\n- Per-User override of the Org default. The model is \"Org owns its config\" per CONTEXT.md.\n- Quick-switch dropdown in the global header. YAGNI for now; one click to the list page is fast enough.\n- RBAC tightening (admin-only mutations). Current behavior — any Org member can mutate — is preserved; tracked as a follow-up.\n- Persisting last-tested-at / last-test-status on the provider row. Surface them in the in-flight UI only; schema work deferred.\n\n## Decisions (grilled, all locked)\n\n| # | Question | Decision | Reason |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Q1 | Default scope | **Single org-wide default** | Schema + code already assume it. Chat/embed leak bug is a model-picker problem, not a provider-scope problem. ADR-0006. |\n| Q2 | Switch action UX | **Instant toggle, optimistic update, rollback toast** | Cheap, reversible, no data loss; existing Create / Delete confirms already saturate the page's modal budget. |\n| Q3 | Edit-in-place shape | **Hybrid — inline for safe fields, modal for credentials** | Honors \"edit-in-place\" spirit (rename, swap model in one click) while preserving the Test-Connection gate for `api_key` / `base_url`. |\n| Q4 | API key edit semantics | **Explicit \"Rotate API key\" disclosure** | Zero ambiguity vs masked-placeholder; no secret-shaped noise on routine edits; aligns with secret-rotation mental model. |\n| Q5 | Default visual indicator | **Amber \"Default\" pill on the card** + \"Make default\" button on non-default cards | Distinct from green `status=active` badge; pill rather than star/radio for legibility. |\n| Q6 | Status & health display | **Keep existing status badge as-is** | Persisting `last_tested_at` is schema work; defer. |\n| Q7 | Menu placement | **AppHeader dropdown (above Sign out) + AppSidebar (desktop)** | Two entry points for two contexts. Settings page button stays as the third path. |\n| Q8 | RBAC | **No change (any Org member can mutate)** | Track admin-only gate as a separate follow-up issue. |\n| Q9 | Header quick-switch dropdown | **No** | YAGNI. |\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Backend (Go, `internal/handler/llm_provider.go` + `internal/service/llm_provider.go`)\n\nTwo changes:\n\n1. **`PUT /api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id`** already exists per `llm_provider_test.go:196`. Audit the handler to confirm it accepts a partial body (only mutates fields present) and never overwrites `api_key` when omitted. Add a regression test that omits `api_key` and asserts the stored ciphertext is unchanged.\n2. **`POST /api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/test`** extends to accept `{provider_id}` *instead of* credentials. When `provider_id` is set, the handler loads the row, decrypts the stored key, and probes with it. This is what the Edit dialog uses when the user hasn't clicked \"Rotate API key\".\n\n### Frontend (Vue 3, `frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue`)\n\nThe page is rewritten around three pieces:\n\n1. **Provider card** (one per row, same component for desktop and mobile, responsive Tailwind):\n   - Header: `display_name` (inline-editable), provider type icon, status badge, **Default pill** (if `is_default`).\n   - Body: provider type label, `base_url` (when set), model (inline `<select>` from `PROVIDER_MODELS[type]`), API key hint (\"configured\" / \"not set\").\n   - Action row: `Make default` button (hidden on the default card), `Edit credentials` button (opens dialog), `Delete` button.\n   - Inline edits (display_name, model) autosave on blur via `updateLlmProvider` and show a brief \"Saved\" tick.\n\n2. **Edit credentials dialog** — same component shape as the Create dialog, two modes:\n   - Default mode: `base_url` editable; **\"Rotate API key\"** button is the only way to reveal an api_key input.\n   - When `base_url` changes OR the rotate input has a value, the dialog **re-runs Test Connection** before allowing Save (mirrors Create's gate, line 215+ in current file).\n   - When neither changed, Save is unblocked and `api_key` is omitted from the PUT body — backend leaves the stored key untouched.\n\n3. **Make-default action**:\n   - Optimistic store mutation: flip `is_default` locally, call `setDefaultLlmProvider`, on failure roll back + toast.\n   - The previously-default card's pill disappears with a 200ms fade; the newly-default card's pill fades in.\n   - A non-blocking warning banner appears inside the card if the user clicks Make-default on a provider whose last in-session test was `fail` (we only know in-session state until Q6 schema work lands).\n\n### Menu wiring\n\n- **`AppHeader.vue`** (`components/AppHeader.vue`): add a `<RouterLink to=\"/llm-providers\">` above the Sign-out button inside the menu. Icon: small chip glyph (Heroicons `cpu-chip` or equivalent inline SVG to match the rest of the file's stroked SVGs).\n- **`AppSidebar.vue`** (`components/AppSidebar.vue`): add an \"AI Providers\" `<RouterLink>` between the existing main-nav items and the Account section. Title `AI Providers`, active-class same as siblings.\n\n## Data flow\n\n```\n                                ┌───────────────────────┐\n                                │   /llm-providers      │\n                                │   LlmProviderListPage │\n                                └────────┬──────────────┘\n                                         │\n                                         ▼\n                            useLlmProvidersStore (Pinia)\n                                         │\n            ┌────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐\n            ▼                            ▼                             ▼\n   GET  /llm-providers       PUT /llm-providers/:id        PUT /llm-providers/:id/default\n   (list, on mount)          (inline + dialog edits)       (Make default, optimistic)\n\n                            POST /llm-providers/test\n                            { provider_id }  ← new shape, used by Edit dialog\n                            { provider, base_url, api_key } ← existing shape (Create + Rotate)\n```\n\n## Glossary additions (in this PR)\n\nCONTEXT.md gains:\n\n- **LLM Provider**: A configured connection (provider type + `base_url` + credentials + a default model) that an Org uses to serve chat and embedding requests. An Org has zero or more.\n- **Default Provider**: The single LLM Provider with `is_default = true`. All chat, embedding, and RAG calls resolve through it unless overridden by an explicit provider slug in the call.\n- **Provider Type**: The vendor family — one of `openai`, `anthropic`, `ollama`, `custom`. Editable only by deleting and recreating.\n\n## Out-of-scope follow-ups\n\n- Persist `last_tested_at` + `last_test_status` on the provider row (schema work).\n- Admin-only RBAC gate on mutations.\n- Per-purpose default split (chat-default vs embed-default). Add a `default_for ENUM` only if a real product need surfaces.\n\n## Issue breakdown (tracer-bullet vertical slices)\n\nSix issues, each independently grabbable and behind-a-flag-free.\n\n### A — Backend: provider Update audit + Test-with-stored-key\n- Audit `PUT /llm-providers/:id` to confirm it preserves `api_key` when omitted; add regression test.\n- Extend `POST /llm-providers/test` to accept `{provider_id}`; when set, decrypt stored key and probe.\n- Unit tests + handler test.\n\n### B — Frontend: Default badge + Make-default action\n- \"Default\" amber pill component on `LlmProviderListPage` cards.\n- \"Make default\" button on non-default cards.\n- Optimistic store mutation; rollback toast on failure.\n- Warning inline-banner if target's in-session test was `fail`.\n\n### C — Frontend: Edit credentials dialog (hybrid inline + modal)\n- Reuse Create-dialog markup as the Edit dialog, pre-filled from card.\n- \"Rotate API key\" disclosure (hidden input until clicked).\n- Re-run Test Connection when `base_url` or rotate input changed; gate Save.\n- Omit `api_key` from PUT body when not rotated.\n\n### D — Frontend: Menu entries\n- Add \"AI Providers\" link to `AppHeader.vue` user-profile dropdown (above Sign out).\n- Add \"AI Providers\" link to `AppSidebar.vue` desktop nav.\n- Icons match existing inline-SVG style.\n\n### E — Frontend: Card redesign + inline edits\n- Refactor desktop + mobile card variants into one responsive component.\n- Inline-editable `display_name` (click-to-edit, autosave on blur).\n- Inline-selectable `model` (`<select>` from `PROVIDER_MODELS[type]`, autosave on change).\n- Show provider type icon, `base_url`, key hint, status, default pill.\n\n### F — E2E Playwright coverage\n- Switch default between two providers; assert pill moves; assert chat call resolves to the new default.\n- Rename inline; reload; assert persisted.\n- Change model inline; reload; assert persisted.\n- Rotate key; assert Test-Connection re-gate; assert Save unlocked only after pass.\n- Cancel-and-rollback toast on a deliberately failing default switch (mocked).\n\n## Success criteria\n\n- User can flip the default between providers in one click and see the pill move within 200ms (optimistic).\n- User can rename a provider, change its model, and rotate its API key without leaving the list page.\n- \"AI Providers\" appears in both the user-profile dropdown and the desktop sidebar.\n- All existing functionality (Create flow with Test Connection gate, Delete with confirm) is untouched.\n- Frontend lint + golangci-lint pass with `--new-from-rev=HEAD` (no new violations).\n- New Playwright scenarios pass headless in CI.\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/jobinlawrance/Project/raven/docs/adr/0006-single-org-wide-llm-provider-default.md",
  "content": "# 0006 — Single org-wide LLM Provider default\n\n**Status:** Accepted\n**Date:** 2026-06-02\n\n## Decision\n\nAn Org has **exactly one default LLM Provider** at a time, represented by the boolean `is_default` on the provider row. Every chat, embedding, and RAG call resolves through this single default unless the caller passes an explicit provider slug.\n\nWe do **not** split the default by purpose (no separate \"chat default\" and \"embed default\"). We do **not** allow per-User overrides of the Org default.\n\n## Why\n\n- The schema and call path already assume a single default. `llm_provider_configs.is_default boolean` is the canonical source; `useLlmProvidersStore.setDefaultLlmProvider` and the `PUT /llm-providers/:id/default` route both treat it as singular. Recent fixes (`fix(chat): resolve org's default LLM provider instead of hardcoding 'anthropic'`, commit `9c4e0d58`) closed the last gap where call paths bypassed it.\n- The recurring chat-vs-embed-leak bug — where a chat model accidentally got passed to the embedding endpoint — was a **model-picker** problem, not a **provider-scope** problem. A single provider config holds both a default chat model and a default embedding model in its `config` JSON; the call site picks which one to use. Splitting the default by purpose would not have prevented that bug.\n- Per-User override breaks the \"Org owns its config\" mental model already established in CONTEXT.md and reinforced by ADR-0005 (Org is the Marketplace publisher). Two members of the same Org should see the same chat behavior; otherwise debugging \"why did this answer differ?\" becomes an opaque per-User config diff.\n- The cost of adding (b) — per-purpose split — later is small and additive: introduce a `default_for ENUM('all','chat','embed')` column, keep `default_for='all'` as the singleton invariant, allow rows with `default_for='chat'` or `'embed'` to coexist. No data loss, no breaking change for current call sites.\n\n## Trade-offs accepted\n\n- **Mixed-vendor stacks need creative model wiring.** A common real-world stack is \"chat via Anthropic, embed via local Ollama.\" Under this decision, the Org's single default provider is one of them, and the *other* call path must pass an explicit provider slug (or look up the right provider by model name). We accept this constraint because the alternative — two defaults — multiplies invariants (what if both are missing? what if both point at the same row? how does the UI surface both?) for a stack shape that is currently exercised by one of our own users (the demo box on Ollama).\n- **Switching the default is a tenant-wide observable.** Org member A flips the default; member B's next chat hits a different vendor. We accept this because (1) all members already share the same `knowledge_bases` and embeddings, so the vendor change does not affect retrieval semantics, only the LLM that synthesizes the answer; (2) the alternative is per-User defaults, which we rejected above.\n- **Auto-defaulting on first create stays.** A fresh Org with zero providers cannot chat (the chat path 500s with \"No active 'X' provider config found\"). The list page already sets `is_default=true` on the first row at create time (`feat(llm): guide users to vendor console + auto-default first provider`, commit `9f8ad6b4`). This decision keeps that behavior.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The list page UI gains a single \"Default\" pill per Org (not multiple pills for chat/embed).\n- The \"Make default\" action on a non-default card flips exactly one boolean — atomic, no per-purpose menu.\n- The `setDefault` endpoint signature stays `PUT /llm-providers/:id/default` with no body. No `?for=chat` query param.\n- If we ever ship per-purpose defaults, the migration is purely additive: add `default_for ENUM` with default `'all'`, keep this row as the only `'all'` row, and add new rows for the new purposes. This ADR will need a sibling.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **(b) Split by purpose: chat-default + embed-default.** Two flags on the provider row (or one `default_for` enum). Rejected: invariants explode (what if both `is_chat_default` rows? what if neither?), and the bug it was supposed to fix is a model-picker issue.\n- **(c) Per-User override.** Each User picks their preferred provider for their session; Org default is the fallback. Rejected: breaks the \"Org owns its config\" mental model and creates per-User opaque divergence.\n"
}
```

```
1	# Raven
2	
3	Multi-tenant RAG platform: orgs upload documents into knowledge bases, query them via chat or widget, and embed grounded answers into third-party apps.
4	
5	## Language
6	
7	**Organization** (Org):
8	The top-level tenant. Owns billing, subscription, members, and all data created beneath it. Identified by `org_id` in RLS and throughout the codebase.
9	_Avoid_: Account, tenant, customer.
10	
11	**Workspace**:
12	A sub-grouping inside an Org that owns one or more Knowledge Bases. Used to scope membership, API keys, and (eventually) per-team plan limits.
13	_Avoid_: Project, team.
14	
15	**Knowledge Base** (KB):
16	A collection of Sources, Documents, Chunks, and their Embeddings against which Chats and Widgets are run. Belongs to exactly one Workspace.
17	_Avoid_: Corpus, dataset, library.
18	
19	**Source**:
20	An input to a KB — uploaded file, URL, connector. Materializes into one or more Documents on processing.
21	
22	**Chunk**:
23	The atomic embeddable unit of text extracted from a Document. Sized by the chunker to fit the embedding model's token window.
24	
25	**Embedding**:
26	A vector for a Chunk produced by an embedding model. Currently `vector(768)` from `nomic-embed-text`.
27	
28	**Subscription**:
29	The billing relationship between an Org and a paid plan. One active subscription per Org. The **Free Plan** is the implicit state when no active paid subscription exists.
30	
31	**Free Plan Org**:
32	An Org without an active paid Subscription. The phrase "free user" is shorthand for "a User belonging to a Free Plan Org" — the plan is a property of the Org, never the User. Free Plan Orgs are governed by the strict-flywheel rule in [ADR-0004](docs/adr/0004-free-tier-public-only-rule.md): every KB they hold — whether created or imported — is forced `visibility=public`.
33	_Avoid_: Free user, free account (when used to imply a per-user concept).
34	
35	**Read-only-private KB**:
36	A KB in the transitional state produced when a Paid Plan Org downgrades to Free Plan. Stays private but cannot accept new Sources, Documents, or Chats until the User Publishes it, Deletes it, or upgrades back. Represented by `kb_status = 'read_only_private'`.
37	
38	**Derivative Public KB**:
39	A Public KB whose `source_public_kb_id` points at another Public KB — i.e. an Imported KB that was itself made public (either because the Importer chose to publish their fork, or because the Importer is a Free Plan Org and the strict-flywheel rule forced publication). Lineage is preserved indefinitely; takedowns of the original do not cascade.
40	
41	### Marketplace
42	
43	**Marketplace**:
44	The cross-tenant discovery surface that lists Public KBs available for Import. Hosted at `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace`. Accessible only to authenticated Users; no anonymous browsing.
45	
46	**Content-grade Publish**:
47	The data boundary applied when a KB is Published or Imported. Chunks, Embeddings, and Source metadata cross the boundary; original file blobs, runtime artefacts (api_keys, chats, routing_rules, webhooks, response_cache, connectors), and any non-allow-listed `settings` keys do not. See [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-content-grade-publish-boundary.md).
48	
49	**Public KB**:
50	A KB whose publishing Org has flipped its `visibility` to `public`, making it discoverable on the Marketplace. The KB itself still lives in its publishing Workspace; visibility is the only thing that changes.
51	
52	**Private KB**:
53	A KB visible only inside its owning Org. The default state for every KB.
54	
55	**Publish**:
56	The act of flipping a KB from `private` to `public`. Reversible (the publisher can unpublish), but unpublish does not affect already-Imported copies. The publisher of record is the **Org**, not the User who pressed the button. See [ADR-0005](docs/adr/0005-org-as-marketplace-publisher.md).
57	
58	**Org slug**:
59	A globally-unique, URL-safe identifier for an Org. Forms the first segment of every Marketplace URL: `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace/{org_slug}/{kb_slug}`. Backfilled from `display_name` at migration; subsequently editable but constrained for uniqueness.
60	
61	**Marketplace URL**:
62	The canonical public address of a Public KB: `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace/{org_slug}/{kb_slug}`. 404s if either slug is unknown or the target is private.
63	
64	**Import**:
65	The act of an Org cloning a Public KB into one of its own Workspaces. Produces an independent KB row with its own Sources, Chunks, and Embeddings — a fork, not a live link. See [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-marketplace-fork-on-import.md).
66	
67	**Re-import**:
68	A destructive overwrite of an existing Imported KB with the publisher's current state. Replaces the Importer's local Chunks and Embeddings; preserves the Importer's KB id, Chats, Widgets, and other runtime artefacts (these FK to the Imported KB id, not its content). Always confirmed.
69	
70	**`last_modified_at`**:
71	Timestamp on a Public KB reflecting the most recent content-affecting change in the publisher's workspace. Shown as "Updated 3 days ago" on Marketplace listings; the Marketplace and Import operations both read live KB state per [ADR-0003](docs/adr/0003-always-fresh-publish-lifecycle.md) — there is no separate publication snapshot in MVP.
72	
73	**`imported_from_revision_at`**:
74	Timestamp stamped on the Importer's local KB at the moment of Import, recording the publisher's `last_modified_at` value captured. Lets the Importer reason about what they have vs what's now available upstream.
75	
76	**Importer Org**:
77	An Org that has Imported one or more Public KBs. Distinct from the **Publishing Org** that owns the original.
78	
79	**License (SPDX)**:
80	A required declaration on every Public KB, chosen from a 7-item allow-list (`CC0-1.0`, `CC-BY-4.0`, `CC-BY-SA-4.0`, `CC-BY-NC-4.0`, `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `GPL-3.0`). Surfaced as a badge on every Marketplace card and Importer-side KB. See [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-licence-and-moderation.md).
81	
82	**Takedown**:
83	The forced or voluntary removal of a Public KB from the Marketplace. Sources: publisher (self-unpublish), DMCA (third-party copyright claim via `dmca@ravencloak.org`), or admin (TOS violation). Does not cascade to Derivative Public KBs; derivative owners are notified instead.
84	
85	**Strike**:
86	A confirmed Takedown attributable to an Org. Three strikes triggers Org-level suspension via admin runbook. Tracked on `organizations.takedown_strikes`.
87	
88	**Preview**:
89	A narrow public surface returning ≤3 sample Chunks from a Public KB, served by a `SECURITY DEFINER` Postgres function so logged-in Users can assess content quality before deciding to Import. The only place Marketplace traffic reads published Chunks cross-tenant — bounded by the function's signature, not a general RLS hole. See [ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-marketplace-lifecycle-behaviours.md).
90	
91	**Discovery**:
92	The browse / search surface at `raven.ravencloak.org/marketplace`. Postgres full-text search over KB metadata (name, description, publishing Org's display name), with sort options (Newest, Most imported, Recently updated, Alphabetic) and a license multi-select filter. No categories, tags, or content search in MVP. See [ADR-0008](docs/adr/0008-marketplace-discovery-and-operations.md).
93	
94	## Relationships
95	
96	- An **Org** has one active **Subscription** (or none, in which case it is a **Free Plan Org**).
97	- An **Org** has many **Workspaces**; each **Workspace** has many **KBs**.
98	- A **KB** has many **Sources**; each **Source** produces many **Documents**; each **Document** produces many **Chunks**; each **Chunk** has one **Embedding**.
99	- A **Public KB** can be **Imported** by many other **Orgs**, producing one **Imported KB** per Importer Org. Imported KBs do not track publisher edits — they are forks at the moment of import.
100	- **Chats** and **Widgets** always belong to the **Importer Org** and FK to the **Imported KB**, never to the publisher's KB.
101	
102	## Example dialogue
103	
104	> **Dev:** "If a user on the **Free Plan** uploads a doc, where does it land?"
105	> **Domain expert:** "Their **Org** is a Free Plan Org, so any **KB** they create has to be **Public**. The doc still uploads into that KB in their **Workspace** like normal — it's just discoverable from the **Marketplace**."
106	
107	> **Dev:** "If the publisher edits the **KB** after I've **Imported** it, do I see the changes?"
108	> **Domain expert:** "No. **Import** is a fork. You'd have to re-import to get the new version."
109	
110	## Flagged ambiguities
111	
112	- "Account" was used to mean both **User** and **Org**. Resolved: **Org** is the billing and data-ownership unit; **User** is a person who is a member of one or more Orgs. "Free account" specifically means **Free Plan Org**.
113
```

## How to handle the docs commits — pick one

**(1) Skip the docs PR entirely. Just create the milestone + issues.**
The spec lives at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-llm-provider-management-design.md` on disk; ADR-0009 lives at `docs/adr/0009-single-org-wide-llm-provider-default.md` on disk. Each GH issue I create will include the relevant spec section inline so the issue is self-contained. I'll revert my CONTEXT.md edit (since it's tangled with the parallel Marketplace glossary).
*Pros:* Zero risk of conflicting with your Marketplace work. Issues are immediately actionable.
*Cons:* The spec + ADR live only on disk; they aren't versioned in the repo until you choose to land them.

**(2) Docs PR for *only my new files* (M13 spec + ADR-0009).**
Branch off `main`, `git add` exclusively the two new files, revert CONTEXT.md, open PR. Marketplace ADRs stay on `entire/cf2c5f4-e3b0c4` untouched.
*Pros:* Spec + ADR get tracked.
*Cons:* CONTEXT.md glossary additions don't land — they'll have to ride with the Marketplace docs PR later. ADR-0009 references CONTEXT.md terms that don't yet exist in the committed tree.

**(3) Docs PR includes Marketplace + M13 (cherry-pick from `entire/cf2c5f4-e3b0c4` + my new files).**
*Pros:* Everything coherent.
*Cons:* I'm landing parallel work you may have a different plan for. Risky.

**My recommendation: (1).** Issues with self-contained bodies are the unit of execution; the spec and ADR are working documents on disk you can land whenever the Marketplace docs are ready. Lowest risk of stepping on your in-flight Marketplace branch.

Pick **(1)**, **(2)**, or **(3)** — then I'll proceed with the milestone + 6 parallel issue-creation agents.

- **Path:** `POST /api/v1/orgs/:org_id/documents/:document_id/reprocess`
- **Handler:** loads the doc (RLS-scoped via existing `db.WithOrgID`), validates it belongs to the caller's org, calls `queue.Client.EnqueueDocumentProcess` with the doc's existing `org_id` + `kb_id`, returns 202 Accepted with the task id.
- **AuthN:** existing SuperTokens middleware. **AuthZ:** gate on org membership (or admin-only once RBAC tightens).

## LLM Provider endpoints

All under `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers`. Bearer auth via SuperTokens session.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers` | List org's providers |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers` | Create provider |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id` | Get one |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id` | Update (omitting `api_key` preserves stored key — PR #749) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id` | Delete |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id/default` | Set as org default (no body) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/test` | Test connection |

### Create body

```json
{
  "provider": "openai|anthropic|ollama|custom",
  "display_name": "my OpenAI",
  "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
  "api_key": "sk-...",
  "config": { "model": "gpt-4o-mini" },
  "is_default": true
}
```

Ollama is keyless — backend accepts `"api_key": "not-required"` as a stub. `base_url` defaults to `http://localhost:11434` if omitted.

### Test connection — two shapes (per PR #749)

**(a) Inline creds** — used by Create dialog and Rotate API key flow:
```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
  "api_key": "sk-..."
}
```

**(b) Stored creds** — used by Edit dialog when user didn't rotate the key:
```json
{
  "provider_id": "uuid-of-existing-provider"
}
```

Response (both shapes):
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "latency_ms": 412,
  "detail": ""
}
```

### Where these live in the code

- Routes wired in `internal/handler/llm_provider.go`
- Service layer: `internal/service/llm_provider.go`
- Frontend client wrapper: `frontend/src/api/llm-providers.ts`
- Pinia store: `frontend/src/stores/llm-providers.ts`

**Define hard enforcement for the singleton default invariant.**

The ADR declares “exactly one default,” but it does not require an enforcement mechanism (e.g., transactional unset+set and/or a DB-level uniqueness strategy scoped to org). Without this, concurrent default switches can produce zero or multiple defaults transiently or persistently.

```
1	# 0009 — Single org-wide LLM Provider default
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Date:** 2026-06-02
5	
6	## Decision
7	
8	An Org has **exactly one default LLM Provider** at a time, represented by the boolean `is_default` on the provider row. Every chat, embedding, and RAG call resolves through this single default unless the caller passes an explicit provider slug.
9	
10	We do **not** split the default by purpose (no separate "chat default" and "embed default"). We do **not** allow per-User overrides of the Org default.
11	
12	## Why
13	
14	- The schema and call path already assume a single default. `llm_provider_configs.is_default boolean` is the canonical source; `useLlmProvidersStore.setDefaultLlmProvider` and the `PUT /llm-providers/:id/default` route both treat it as singular. Recent fixes (`fix(chat): resolve org's default LLM provider instead of hardcoding 'anthropic'`, commit `9c4e0d58`) closed the last gap where call paths bypassed it.
15	- The recurring chat-vs-embed-leak bug — where a chat model accidentally got passed to the embedding endpoint — was a **model-picker** problem, not a **provider-scope** problem. A single provider config holds both a default chat model and a default embedding model in its `config` JSON; the call site picks which one to use. Splitting the default by purpose would not have prevented that bug.
16	- Per-User override breaks the "Org owns its config" mental model already established in CONTEXT.md and reinforced by ADR-0005 (Org is the Marketplace publisher). Two members of the same Org should see the same chat behavior; otherwise debugging "why did this answer differ?" becomes an opaque per-User config diff.
17	- The cost of adding (b) — per-purpose split — later is small and additive: introduce a `default_for ENUM('all','chat','embed')` column, keep `default_for='all'` as the singleton invariant, allow rows with `default_for='chat'` or `'embed'` to coexist. No data loss, no breaking change for current call sites.
18	
19	## Trade-offs accepted
20	
21	- **Mixed-vendor stacks need creative model wiring.** A common real-world stack is "chat via Anthropic, embed via local Ollama." Under this decision, the Org's single default provider is one of them, and the *other* call path must pass an explicit provider slug (or look up the right provider by model name). We accept this constraint because the alternative — two defaults — multiplies invariants (what if both are missing? what if both point at the same row? how does the UI surface both?) for a stack shape that is currently exercised by one of our own users (the demo box on Ollama).
22	- **Switching the default is a tenant-wide observable.** Org member A flips the default; member B's next chat hits a different vendor. We accept this because (1) all members already share the same `knowledge_bases` and embeddings, so the vendor change does not affect retrieval semantics, only the LLM that synthesizes the answer; (2) the alternative is per-User defaults, which we rejected above.
23	- **Auto-defaulting on first create stays.** A fresh Org with zero providers cannot chat (the chat path 500s with "No active 'X' provider config found"). The list page already sets `is_default=true` on the first row at create time (`feat(llm): guide users to vendor console + auto-default first provider`, commit `9f8ad6b4`). This decision keeps that behavior.
24	
25	## Consequences
26	
27	- The list page UI gains a single "Default" pill per Org (not multiple pills for chat/embed).
28	- The "Make default" action on a non-default card flips exactly one boolean — atomic, no per-purpose menu.
29	- The `setDefault` endpoint signature stays `PUT /llm-providers/:id/default` with no body. No `?for=chat` query param.
30	- If we ever ship per-purpose defaults, the migration is purely additive: add `default_for ENUM` with default `'all'`, keep this row as the only `'all'` row, and add new rows for the new purposes. This ADR will need a sibling.
31	
32	## Alternatives considered
33	
34	- **(b) Split by purpose: chat-default + embed-default.** Two flags on the provider row (or one `default_for` enum). Rejected: invariants explode (what if both `is_chat_default` rows? what if neither?), and the bug it was supposed to fix is a model-picker issue.
35	- **(c) Per-User override.** Each User picks their preferred provider for their session; Org default is the fallback. Rejected: breaks the "Org owns its config" mental model and creates per-User opaque divergence.
36	
```

45	## Architecture
46	
47	### Backend (Go, `internal/handler/llm_provider.go` + `internal/service/llm_provider.go`)
48	
49	Two changes:
50	
51	1. **`PUT /api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/:provider_id`** already exists per `llm_provider_test.go:196`. Audit the handler to confirm it accepts a partial body (only mutates fields present) and never overwrites `api_key` when omitted. Add a regression test that omits `api_key` and asserts the stored ciphertext is unchanged.
52	2. **`POST /api/v1/orgs/:org_id/llm-providers/test`** extends to accept `{provider_id}` *instead of* credentials. When `provider_id` is set, the handler loads the row, decrypts the stored key, and probes with it. This is what the Edit dialog uses when the user hasn't clicked "Rotate API key".
53	
54	### Frontend (Vue 3, `frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue`)
55	
56	The page is rewritten around three pieces:
57	
58	1. **Provider card** (one per row, same component for desktop and mobile, responsive Tailwind):
59	   - Header: `display_name` (inline-editable), provider type icon, status badge, **Default pill** (if `is_default`).
60	   - Body: provider type label, `base_url` (when set), model (inline `<select>` from `PROVIDER_MODELS[type]`), API key hint ("configured" / "not set").
61	   - Action row: `Make default` button (hidden on the default card), `Edit credentials` button (opens dialog), `Delete` button.
62	   - Inline edits (display_name, model) autosave on blur via `updateLlmProvider` and show a brief "Saved" tick.
63	
64	2. **Edit credentials dialog** — same component shape as the Create dialog, two modes:
65	   - Default mode: `base_url` editable; **"Rotate API key"** button is the only way to reveal an api_key input.
66	   - When `base_url` changes OR the rotate input has a value, the dialog **re-runs Test Connection** before allowing Save (mirrors Create's gate, line 215+ in current file).
67	   - When neither changed, Save is unblocked and `api_key` is omitted from the PUT body — backend leaves the stored key untouched.
68	
69	3. **Make-default action**:
70	   - Optimistic store mutation: flip `is_default` locally, call `setDefaultLlmProvider`, on failure roll back + toast.
71	   - The previously-default card's pill disappears with a 200ms fade; the newly-default card's pill fades in.
72	   - A non-blocking warning banner appears inside the card if the user clicks Make-default on a provider whose last in-session test was `fail` (we only know in-session state until Q6 schema work lands).
73	
74	### Menu wiring
75	
76	- **`AppHeader.vue`** (`components/AppHeader.vue`): add a `<RouterLink to="/llm-providers">` above the Sign-out button inside the menu. Icon: small chip glyph (Heroicons `cpu-chip` or equivalent inline SVG to match the rest of the file's stroked SVGs).
77	- **`AppSidebar.vue`** (`components/AppSidebar.vue`): add an "AI Providers" `<RouterLink>` between the existing main-nav items and the Account section. Title `AI Providers`, active-class same as siblings.
78	
79	## Data flow

81	```
82	                                ┌───────────────────────┐
83	                                │   /llm-providers      │
84	                                │   LlmProviderListPage │
85	                                └────────┬──────────────┘
86	                                         │
87	                                         ▼
88	                            useLlmProvidersStore (Pinia)
89	                                         │
90	            ┌────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
91	            ▼                            ▼                             ▼
92	   GET  /llm-providers       PUT /llm-providers/:id        PUT /llm-providers/:id/default
93	   (list, on mount)          (inline + dialog edits)       (Make default, optimistic)
94	
95	                            POST /llm-providers/test
96	                            { provider_id }  ← new shape, used by Edit dialog
97	                            { provider, base_url, api_key } ← existing shape (Create + Rotate)
98	```
99	
100	## Glossary additions (in this PR)
101	
102	CONTEXT.md gains:
103	
104	- **LLM Provider**: A configured connection (provider type + `base_url` + credentials + a default model) that an Org uses to serve chat and embedding requests. An Org has zero or more.
105	- **Default Provider**: The single LLM Provider with `is_default = true`. All chat, embedding, and RAG calls resolve through it unless overridden by an explicit provider slug in the call.
106	- **Provider Type**: The vendor family — one of `openai`, `anthropic`, `ollama`, `custom`. Editable only by deleting and recreating.
107	
108	## Out-of-scope follow-ups
109	
110	- Persist `last_tested_at` + `last_test_status` on the provider row (schema work).
111	- Admin-only RBAC gate on mutations.
112	- Per-purpose default split (chat-default vs embed-default). Add a `default_for ENUM` only if a real product need surfaces.
113

115	
116	Six issues, each independently grabbable and behind-a-flag-free.

131	- "Rotate API key" disclosure (hidden input until clicked).
132	- Re-run Test Connection when `base_url` or rotate input changed; gate Save.

137	- Add "AI Providers" link to `AppSidebar.vue` desktop nav.
138	- Icons match existing inline-SVG style.

143	- Inline-selectable `model` (`<select>` from `PROVIDER_MODELS[type]`, autosave on change).

```json
  "old_string": "We do **not** split the default by purpose (no separate \"chat default\" and \"embed default\"). We do **not** allow per-User overrides of the Org default.\n\n## Why",
  "new_string": "We do **not** split the default by purpose (no separate \"chat default\" and \"embed default\"). We do **not** allow per-User overrides of the Org default.\n\n## Enforcement of the singleton invariant\n\nThe \"exactly one default per Org\" rule is upheld by **two coordinated mechanisms** — DB-level and application-level — because either alone leaves a race window:\n\n1. **Partial unique index on the provider table.** A filtered/partial unique index on `llm_provider_configs (org_id) WHERE is_default = true` makes it impossible to commit two rows with `is_default = true` for the same `org_id`. This is the floor: even a buggy or malicious writer cannot create two defaults.\n2. **Transactional `set_default_provider` operation.** Switching the default is a single transaction that (a) `UPDATE … SET is_default = false WHERE org_id = $1 AND is_default = true` and (b) `UPDATE … SET is_default = true WHERE org_id = $1 AND id = $2`, in that order, in one BEGIN/COMMIT. Callers MUST use this operation; ad-hoc UPDATEs that set `is_default = true` without first clearing the existing default will be rejected by the partial unique index, which is desirable (fail fast) but a poor user-facing error — so the transactional helper is the only sanctioned path.\n\nTogether these guarantee that at every committed point in time, an Org has **zero or one** row with `is_default = true`. The \"zero\" case is the bootstrap state for a fresh Org (no providers yet) — addressed by auto-defaulting the first created provider (see Trade-offs accepted below).\n\n## Why"
}
```

> AGENT

## What's blocking

| Setting on `main` | Value |
|---|---|
| `required_approving_review_count` | 0 (no approvals required) |
| `dismiss_stale_reviews` | true |

GitHub's `dismiss_stale_reviews` **only** dismisses approving reviews automatically when new commits land — not `CHANGES_REQUESTED` reviews. CodeRabbit's stale review from before my fix-up commit still stands, and any reviewer-with-write-access requesting changes blocks merge regardless of the approval-count setting.

## Action taken

Posted `@coderabbitai review` on the PR. CodeRabbit usually responds within a couple of minutes — it'll re-scan the latest commit and either approve or post fresh findings. If it approves, the block lifts and auto-merge fires.

## If CodeRabbit doesn't respond fast (fallback)

Two ways to dismiss the stale review:

- **GitHub UI:** PR page → top of CodeRabbit's review block → ⋯ menu → **Dismiss review**. You need the dismissal reason (one-liner like "Addressed in 0971ec6a").
- **Via `gh` CLI** (let me run this if you want):
  ```
  gh api repos/ravencloak-org/Raven/pulls/754/reviews/4412767091/dismissals \
    -X PUT \
    -f message='Addressed in 0971ec6a — re-review requested.'
  ```

Want me to dismiss the review now, or hold a few minutes for CodeRabbit to re-scan?
