commit f7a530ba858ff4b28ec737ee0e598065395833ee
Author: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue May 26 23:02:08 2026 +0530

    feat(llm): tunnel hint for Ollama on remote Raven with localhost URL
    
    When the user picks Ollama in the Add-Provider dialog and types a
    loopback Base URL — http://localhost:11434, 127.0.0.1, [::1], 0.0.0.0 —
    AND the Raven origin itself is NOT loopback (i.e., they're on the
    hosted demo, not self-hosted / Tauri), show an inline hint with two
    copy-able one-liners to expose Ollama publicly:
    
      cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:11434
      ngrok http 11434
    
    Plus a security note that the tunnel exposes the daemon to anyone with
    the URL. Both gates matter:
      - If Base URL isn't loopback, the user's already pointing at
        something the server can reach.
      - If Raven itself is on localhost, the loopback Ollama works as-is.
    
    Cloudflare is listed first because it needs no account and matches
    the cloudflared Raven already uses for its own tunneling.
    
    Copy-to-clipboard uses navigator.clipboard.writeText with a try/catch
    fallback (older browsers / restrictive permissions surface the command
    in the UI instead).
    
    Signed-off-by: Jobin Lawrance <jobinlawrance@gmail.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: 7c50cbe9575a

diff --git a/frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue b/frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue
index fe832b35..efb14095 100644
--- a/frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue
+++ b/frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue
@@ -143,6 +143,69 @@ async function handleCreate() {
 
 const currentProviderHelp = computed(() => providerHelp[form.value.provider])
 
+// Tunnel suggestions shown in the Ollama branch so a user on the
+// hosted demo (whose Vultr box can't reach `localhost`) has a one-liner
+// to expose their local daemon publicly. Cloudflare's `trycloudflare`
+// mode is the recommended first option — no account, no install of
+// anything Raven-side, free, auto-TLS. ngrok is the fallback for users
+// who already have it set up.
+const ollamaTunnels: { label: string; command: string; note?: string }[] = [
+  {
+    label: 'Cloudflare Tunnel (recommended)',
+    command: 'cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:11434',
+    note: 'Prints an https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL. No account needed. Paste it into Base URL above.',
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'ngrok',
+    command: 'ngrok http 11434',
+    note: 'Free account required for stable URLs. Use the https Forwarding address.',
+  },
+]
+
+const copied = ref<string | null>(null)
+async function copyTunnel(command: string) {
+  try {
+    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(command)
+    copied.value = command
+    setTimeout(() => (copied.value === command ? (copied.value = null) : null), 1500)
+  } catch {
+    // Clipboard access can fail under restrictive permissions / older
+    // browsers — surface the command in the UI and let the user copy
+    // it manually instead of throwing.
+    copied.value = null
+  }
+}
+
+// True only when a loopback Base URL is paired with a non-loopback
+// browser origin — i.e., the user typed `http://localhost:...` while
+// hitting Raven on a real public host (demo.ravencloak.org, etc.).
+// On Raven-running-locally (desktop / self-host) the loopback address
+// works as-is and the tunnel hint would be noise.
+const isLoopbackBaseURL = computed(() => {
+  const raw = (form.value.base_url ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
+  if (!raw) return false
+  return (
+    raw.startsWith('http://localhost') ||
+    raw.startsWith('https://localhost') ||
+    raw.startsWith('http://127.') ||
+    raw.startsWith('https://127.') ||
+    raw.startsWith('http://[::1]') ||
+    raw.startsWith('https://[::1]') ||
+    raw.startsWith('http://0.0.0.0') ||
+    raw.startsWith('https://0.0.0.0')
+  )
+})
+
+const ravenHost = computed(() => window.location.hostname)
+const ravenIsRemote = computed(() => {
+  const host = ravenHost.value
+  return host !== 'localhost' && host !== '127.0.0.1' && host !== '[::1]' && host !== '0.0.0.0'
+})
+
+const showTunnelHint = computed(
+  () => form.value.provider === 'ollama' && isLoopbackBaseURL.value && ravenIsRemote.value,
```

410	  editError.value = ''

442	// Tunnel suggestions shown in the Ollama branch so a user on the
443	// hosted demo (whose Vultr box can't reach `localhost`) has a one-liner
444	// to expose their local daemon publicly. Cloudflare's `trycloudflare`
445	// mode is the recommended first option — no account, no install of
446	// anything Raven-side, free, auto-TLS. ngrok is the fallback for users
447	// who already have it set up.
448	const ollamaTunnels: { label: string; command: string; note?: string }[] = [
449	  {
450	    label: 'Cloudflare Tunnel (recommended)',
451	    command: 'cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:11434',
452	    note: 'Prints an https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL. No account needed. Paste it into Base URL above.',
453	  },
454	  {
455	    label: 'ngrok',
456	    command: 'ngrok http 11434',
457	    note: 'Free account required for stable URLs. Use the https Forwarding address.',
458	  },
459	]
460	
461	const copied = ref<string | null>(null)
462	async function copyTunnel(command: string) {
463	  try {
464	    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(command)
465	    copied.value = command
466	    setTimeout(() => (copied.value === command ? (copied.value = null) : null), 1500)
467	  } catch {
468	    // Clipboard access can fail under restrictive permissions / older
469	    // browsers — surface the command in the UI and let the user copy
470	    // it manually instead of throwing.
471	    copied.value = null
472	  }
473	}
474	
475	// True only when a loopback Base URL is paired with a non-loopback
476	// browser origin — i.e., the user typed `http://localhost:...` while
477	// hitting Raven on a real public host (demo.ravencloak.org, etc.).
478	// On Raven-running-locally (desktop / self-host) the loopback address
479	// works as-is and the tunnel hint would be noise.
480	const isLoopbackBaseURL = computed(() => {
481	  const raw = (form.value.base_url ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
482	  if (!raw) return false
483	  return (
484	    raw.startsWith('http://localhost') ||
485	    raw.startsWith('https://localhost') ||
486	    raw.startsWith('http://127.') ||
487	    raw.startsWith('https://127.') ||
488	    raw.startsWith('http://[::1]') ||
489	    raw.startsWith('https://[::1]') ||
490	    raw.startsWith('http://0.0.0.0') ||
491	    raw.startsWith('https://0.0.0.0')
492	  )
493	})
494	
495	const ravenHost = computed(() => window.location.hostname)
496	const ravenIsRemote = computed(() => {
497	  const host = ravenHost.value
498	  return host !== 'localhost' && host !== '127.0.0.1' && host !== '[::1]' && host !== '0.0.0.0'
499	})
500	
501	const showTunnelHint = computed(
502	  () => form.value.provider === 'ollama' && isLoopbackBaseURL.value && ravenIsRemote.value,
503	)
504

-- to a specific dimension. Running outside a transaction lets us use
-- DROP/CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY so this migration is safe to replay
-- on a live table once embeddings have been backfilled.
--
-- Other supported embedding models and their dimensions, for the day
-- someone needs to retune:
--   text-embedding-3-small        1536
--   text-embedding-3-large        3072
--   mxbai-embed-large (Ollama)    1024
--   nomic-embed-text (Ollama)      768  ← we're standardising here
--
-- Going forward the same constant lives in:
--   ai-worker/raven_worker/providers/ollama_provider.py:_DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS
--   ai-worker/raven_worker/providers/registry.py:_DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODELS
--   internal/jobs/document_process.go (when the embed call lands)

-- Bound any lock waits so a long-running ALTER TABLE can't queue behind
-- a slow reader and stall the whole table for hours.
SET lock_timeout = '5s';
SET statement_timeout = '10min';

DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS idx_embeddings_hnsw;

-- The table is empty at the time this migration ships; the drop+add is
-- the simplest path to change a pgvector dimension. If this migration
-- is ever back-ported to a populated cluster, replace this block with
-- an additive column + backfill (see ban-drop-column note from the
-- migration linter).
ALTER TABLE embeddings DROP COLUMN embedding;
ALTER TABLE embeddings ADD COLUMN embedding vector(768) NOT NULL;

-- Recreate the HNSW cosine index at the new dimension. The m/ef_construction
-- params mirror the original (m=16, ef_construction=64) which are the
-- pgvector defaults for "good recall, modest build time".
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_embeddings_hnsw ON embeddings
USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);

-- +goose Down
SET lock_timeout = '5s';
SET statement_timeout = '10min';
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS idx_embeddings_hnsw;
ALTER TABLE embeddings DROP COLUMN embedding;
ALTER TABLE embeddings ADD COLUMN embedding vector(1536) NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_embeddings_hnsw ON embeddings
USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);
```

const API_BASE = () => import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? '/api/v1'

async function authFetch<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(API_BASE() + path, {
    ...init,
    credentials: 'include',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      ...init?.headers,
    },
  })
  if (!res.ok) {
    const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({}))
    throw new Error(data.message || data.error || `Request failed (${res.status})`)
  }
  return res.json()
}

export async function listLlmProviders(orgId: string): Promise<LlmProvider[]> {
  const data = await authFetch<LlmProvider[] | { items: LlmProvider[] }>(
    `/orgs/${orgId}/llm-providers`,
  )
  return Array.isArray(data) ? data : (data.items ?? [])
}

export async function createLlmProvider(
  orgId: string,
  data: CreateLlmProviderRequest,
): Promise<LlmProvider> {
  return authFetch<LlmProvider>(`/orgs/${orgId}/llm-providers`, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify(data),
  })
}

  orgId: string,

func countEmbeddedMigrations() (int, error) {
	entries, err := fs.ReadDir(migrations.FS, ".")
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	count := 0
	for _, e := range entries {
		if !e.IsDir() && strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".sql") {
			count++
		}
	}
	return count, nil
}

Actually the situation is more nuanced than I thought. Demo's `goose_db_version` is missing **46**, not 51:

- **Applied on demo (goose):** {1–45, 47–50, 52, 53} = 51 versions
- **Embedded files on main:** {1–45, 46, 47–50, 52, 53} = 52 files
- Mismatch: demo missed applying 00046 (because the embeddings-resize was hot-deployed manually before #689 landed it as a file, then no one ever ran goose-up against the existing schema)

51 is a phantom — neither a file nor an applied row. The real bug is 46 missing from demo's goose.

1. **Code:** Change `VerifyMigrationsState` from count-based to **set-based** comparison so a future numbering hiccup (intentional gap, version skipped) doesn't crash boot. The current `count(*) != fileCount` is fragile.
2. **Data:** Backfill demo's `goose_db_version` with a `(46, is_applied=true)` row so the existing demo Postgres reconciles. The 00046 migration is a no-op on this DB because the schema is already at vector(768) from the prior hot-deploy.

## Endpoint to test Bug 1 fix (SetDefault)

Two ways:

### A) End-to-end via the UI (easiest)
1. Open https://demo.ravencloak.org/raven/
2. Sign in
3. Go to `/llm-providers` (sidebar → AI Providers, or avatar dropdown → AI Providers)
4. If you have 2+ providers, click "Make default" on a non-default card
5. **Expected:** pill moves cleanly, no "Could not switch default" toast.
   **Caveat:** the frontend SPA on demo is from before the fix; but Bug 1 was purely backend (`.json()` failing on empty body) — the v3 binary now returns 200 + body, so `.json()` succeeds even on the stale SPA. You should NOT see the toast anymore.

### B) Direct API check (cURL, needs your session cookie)

```
PUT https://demo.ravencloak.REDACTED<provider_id>/default
```

- **Before fix:** `204 No Content`, empty body.
- **After fix (now):** `200 OK`, body is the full updated `LlmProvider` JSON with `is_default: true`.

Quickest cURL test from your browser session: open DevTools → Network → trigger the action once → copy the request as cURL → re-run it from a terminal. The status line and response body will reveal whether the v3 binary is what's responding.

Anonymous probe (no cookie) currently returns `401` — confirms the route is registered and reachable on the v3 binary.

## Q1 — Scope of "login with passkey"

You said it should live in *Settings → Authentication* AND let users *log in* with passkey. That combines two distinct pieces of work. Pick one:

**(A) Both at once** — Settings → Authentication tab where users **enrol** passkeys (register one for the current device, list, delete), AND a "Sign in with Passkey" button on the login page that uses an enrolled passkey to start the session.

**(B) Enrolment only now** — Settings → Authentication tab to enrol/manage. Sign-in flow stays Google-only for this PR; "Sign in with Passkey" arrives in a follow-up. Users can register a passkey but can't yet use it. (Useful if you want to ship the management UX first and observe.)

**(C) Sign-in only, no Settings UI** — Add "Sign in with Passkey" to the login dialog using browser-side resident keys; no separate Settings management. (Unconventional and probably worse — there's no way to revoke a lost device.)

**My recommendation: (A) — both at once.** Reasons:
- You explicitly said "login with passkey", which implies the sign-in path needs to actually work, not just enrolment.
- Splitting (B) ships a feature whose value is invisible until the second PR lands — users add a passkey, get no benefit, lose confidence.
- (C) leaves you with no recovery surface for a lost device. Bad security UX.

The work in (A) is roughly: 1 new Settings tab + ~3 backend endpoints (register-options, register-verify, list/delete) + 2 sign-in endpoints (assert-options, assert-verify) + the login page button. SuperTokens has a Webauthn recipe that wraps most of this (next question covers whether your current SuperTokens versions ship it).

**Pick (A), (B), or (C)?**

### Register Passkey with Sign Up

Source: https://context7.com/supertokens/supertokens-web-js/llms.txt

Registers a new WebAuthn credential and performs user sign-up in one flow. Includes a browser support check.

```javascript
import { registerCredentialWithSignUp, doesBrowserSupportWebAuthn } from "supertokens-web-js/recipe/webauthn";

async function signUpWithPasskey(email) {
    const support = await doesBrowserSupportWebAuthn({ userContext: {} });
    if (support.status !== "OK" || !support.browserSupportsWebauthn) {
        console.error("WebAuthn not supported");
        return;
    }

    const response = await registerCredentialWithSignUp({
        email,
        userContext: {}
    });

    if (response.status === "OK") {
        console.log("Signed up with passkey:", response.user.id);
        window.location.href = "/dashboard";
    } else if (response.status === "EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS_ERROR") {
        console.error("Email already registered");
    } else if (response.status === "WEBAUTHN_NOT_SUPPORTED") {
        console.error("Browser does not support WebAuthn");
    } else if (response.status === "AUTHENTICATOR_ALREADY_REGISTERED") {
        console.error("This passkey is already registered");
    }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Authenticate with Passkey

Source: https://context7.com/supertokens/supertokens-web-js/llms.txt

Authenticates an existing user using their registered WebAuthn passkey credential.

```javascript
import { authenticateCredentialWithSignIn } from "supertokens-web-js/recipe/webauthn";

async function signInWithPasskey() {
    const response = await authenticateCredentialWithSignIn({
        userContext: {}
    });

    if (response.status === "OK") {
        console.log("Signed in with passkey:", response.user.id);
        window.location.href = "/dashboard";
    } else if (response.status === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR") {
        console.error("Invalid passkey");
    } else if (response.status === "WEBAUTHN_NOT_SUPPORTED") {
        console.error("Browser does not support WebAuthn");
    }
}
```

## POST /supertokens/webauthn/registerCredentialWithSignUp

### Description
Registers a new passkey and signs up the user in a single flow.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
/supertokens/webauthn/registerCredentialWithSignUp

### Parameters
#### Request Body
- **email** (string) - Required - The email address of the user.
- **userContext** (object) - Optional - Contextual information for the user.

### Request Example
```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "userContext": {}
}
```

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **status** (string) - Indicates the status of the operation ('OK' or 'EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS_ERROR', 'WEBAUTHN_NOT_SUPPORTED', 'AUTHENTICATOR_ALREADY_REGISTERED').
- **user** (object) - The user object.
  - **id** (string) - The unique identifier of the user.

#### Response Example
```json
{
  "status": "OK",
  "user": {
    "id": "user-id-123"
  }
}
```

### supertokens.Init — Initialize the SDK

Source: https://context7.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/llms.txt

Bootstraps the SuperTokens SDK with application info, a connection to the core service, and a list of enabled recipe modules. Must be called before any other SDK function.

```APIDOC
## supertokens.Init — Initialize the SDK

### Description
Bootstraps the SuperTokens SDK with application info, a connection to the core service, and a list of enabled recipe modules. Must be called before any other SDK function.

### Usage
```go
package main

import (
    "net/http"

    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/emailpassword"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/emailverification"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/emailverification/evmodels"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/session"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/dashboard"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/supertokens"
)

func main() {
    err := supertokens.Init(supertokens.TypeInput{
        Supertokens: &supertokens.ConnectionInfo{
            ConnectionURI: "http://localhost:3567", // self-hosted core
            APIKey:        "your-api-key",          // if core has an API key set
        },
        AppInfo: supertokens.AppInfo{
            AppName:       "My App",
            APIDomain:     "http://localhost:8080",
            WebsiteDomain: "http://localhost:3000",
            APIBasePath:   strPtr("/auth"), // optional, default is "/auth"
        },
        RecipeList: []supertokens.Recipe{
            emailverification.Init(evmodels.TypeInput{
                Mode: evmodels.ModeRequired,
            }),
            emailpassword.Init(nil),
            session.Init(nil),
            dashboard.Init(nil),
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    http.ListenAndServe(":8080", supertokens.Middleware(http.DefaultServeMux))
}

func strPtr(s string) *string { return &s }
```
```

## emailpassword.SignUp / SignIn — Email+Password Authentication

Registers a new user or authenticates an existing one with email and password credentials.

```go
import (
    "fmt"

    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/emailpassword"
)

func registerUser(email, password string) error {
    result, err := emailpassword.SignUp("public", email, password)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if result.EmailAlreadyExistsError != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("email already registered")
    }
    fmt.Printf("New user created: %s\n", result.OK.User.ID)
    return nil
}

func authenticateUser(email, password string) (string, error) {
    result, err := emailpassword.SignIn("public", email, password)
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    if result.WrongCredentialsError != nil {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid credentials")
    }
    return result.OK.User.ID, nil
}
```

### session.CreateNewSession

Source: https://context7.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/llms.txt

Creates a new session for a user after successful authentication. This function sets the necessary access and refresh token cookies or headers. It's typically called once a user has logged in or signed up.

```APIDOC
## session.CreateNewSession — Create a Session

Creates a new session after successful authentication, setting access/refresh token cookies (or headers). Called once a user is authenticated.

```go
import (
    "net/http"

    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/emailpassword"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/recipe/session"
    "github.com/supertokens/supertokens-golang/supertokens"
)

func loginHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    email := r.FormValue("email")
    password := r.FormValue("password")

    result, err := emailpassword.SignIn("public", email, password)
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500)
        return
    }
    if result.WrongCredentialsError != nil {
        http.Error(w, "Invalid credentials", 401)
        return
    }

    // Create a new session for the authenticated user
    _, err = session.CreateNewSession(
        r, w,
        "public",          // tenantId
        result.OK.User.ID, // userId
        map[string]interface{}{
            "role": "admin",
        }, // accessTokenPayload (embedded in JWT)
        map[string]interface{}{
            "signupDate": "2024-01-01",
        }, // sessionDataInDatabase (server-side only)
    )
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500)
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(200)
    w.Write([]byte("Login successful"))
}
```

Critical fact-check done:

- **`supertokens-golang` (master) ships NO webauthn recipe.** Available recipes: `dashboard, emailpassword, emailverification, jwt, multitenancy, openid, passwordless, session, thirdparty, usermetadata, userroles`. None for WebAuthn.
- **`supertokens-web-js@0.16.0` (what you have) DOES include `/recipe/webauthn`.** Verified — module resolves.
- Your existing `SuperTokensMiddleware` already proxies all `/auth/*` to the core, so `/auth/webauthn/*` should pass through without any new Go recipe code.

That sets up Q2 cleanly:

## Q2 — Implementation approach

**(A) Use SuperTokens' built-in Webauthn recipe.** Frontend adds `Webauthn.init()` alongside `Session` + `ThirdParty`. The recipe's `getRegisterOptions` / `createCredential` / `authenticateCredentialWithSignIn` calls go to `/auth/webauthn/*` on the Go API → middleware proxies to the SuperTokens core → core stores credentials in its own DB. Go-side changes are minimal: just a small hook to sync our local `users` table on first passkey sign-in (mirrors the existing Google ThirdParty path at `internal/handler/auth.go:86`).

**(B) Roll our own with `github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn` (Go library).** Implement custom endpoints, store credentials in our own Postgres table. SuperTokens isn't involved in the passkey flow.

**(C) Wait for `supertokens-golang` to ship a Webauthn recipe.** Don't build.

**My recommendation: (A) — use SuperTokens' built-in Webauthn recipe.** Reasons:
- web-js already has it; we're not pulling a new library on the frontend.
- Core proxy via `SuperTokensMiddleware` exists today — `/auth/webauthn/*` paths flow through without writing a Go-side webauthn wrapper.
- Zero new Raven DB tables (SuperTokens core owns credential storage). One less RLS surface to maintain.
- Consistent with the Google ThirdParty pattern: SuperTokens core is the source of truth for auth artifacts; our `users` table holds Raven-specific metadata, keyed by `external_id`. Same mapping logic on first sign-in.
- (B) duplicates auth state outside SuperTokens — splits source-of-truth, the exact problem the Zitadel→SuperTokens switch was meant to resolve (per `project_zitadel_failure.md`).
- (C) is "don't ship".

**One open question on (A) — risk to flag:** Your docker-compose pulls `registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql` with **no version tag** (so `:latest`). SuperTokens core added the WebAuthn endpoints in a specific version. Before shipping I'd verify the running core actually exposes them (a quick `GET /apiVersion` on the core suffices). If the core is too old we pin to a newer image first. That's a small precondition, not a blocker.

**Pick (A), (B), or (C)?**

> DEVELOPER

A

> AGENT

## Q3 — Multi-passkey policy

How many passkeys can a single user enrol?

**(A) One at a time.** Enrolling a new passkey replaces the existing one. Simplest UI: single "Register passkey for this device" button + "Remove passkey" if one exists. Bad UX for multi-device users (MacBook + iPhone + work laptop).

**(B) Multiple, with user-given labels.** Each passkey row shows label ("MacBook Touch ID"), created-at, last-used-at, with a Remove button. User can add as many as they want. Standard pattern — GitHub, Google, Apple all do this.

**(C) Multiple, no labels.** Just credential IDs + created-at. Spartan; users can't tell which device a passkey corresponds to when revoking.

**My recommendation: (B) — multiple, labeled.**
Reasons:
- SuperTokens' WebAuthn recipe supports multiple credentials per user natively (each row in the core's credential table).
- Real users want to enrol from each of their devices. (A) makes that impossible without re-enrolling every time.
- Labels are essential for revocation. Without them, a user looking at "Passkey from Jun 4" has to guess whether that was their phone or their old laptop. (C) is technically functional but invites mistakes.
- Implementation cost vs (C) is one extra text input on enrolment + one extra column on the list. Trivial.

Edge cases worth naming:
- **Default label**: pre-fill with platform detection (`navigator.userAgent` → "MacBook · Chrome 142" or similar). User can override before save.
- **Cap**: I'd cap at e.g. 10 per user to bound storage. Most users have ≤ 3; the cap is a sanity guard, not a friction point.

**Pick (A), (B), or (C)?**

> DEVELOPER

B

> AGENT

## Q4 — Login page UX

How does the user trigger "sign in with passkey" on the login page?

**(A) Two buttons side by side.** "Sign in with Google" + "Sign in with Passkey". User clicks whichever. Click "Sign in with Passkey" → browser opens its passkey picker (any credential for `demo.ravencloak.org`/`*.ravencloak.org`) → done. No email input required because passkeys are origin-scoped, not user-scoped.

**(B) Email-first conditional UI.** Login page shows an email input. If the email has passkeys → browser auto-prompts; else falls back to Google. Modern Apple/Microsoft pattern. Requires restructuring the login page and an "email lookup" API.

**(C) Auto-prompt on page load + Google fallback.** Login page loads, browser auto-pops the passkey picker via WebAuthn's conditional mediation. Cancel/no-passkey → Google button shows. Most frictionless for returning passkey users; can feel jumpy for first-timers.

**My recommendation: (A) — two buttons.** Reasons:
- Minimal change to the current login page (one extra button next to Google sign-in).
- Passkeys are origin-scoped, so we don't need email input — the browser already knows which credentials match `*.ravencloak.org`.
- Conditional UI (B/C) is the eventual best practice but requires more frontend work AND an unauthenticated "does this email have a passkey?" endpoint, which has user-enumeration concerns (responding `true`/`false` per email leaks account existence).
- (A) keeps Google as the obvious entry for users who haven't enrolled yet; passkey is purely additive.
- Easy to upgrade later: once (A) ships and we have telemetry on usage, adding conditional UI on top is a small follow-up.

**One implementation detail to flag now:** SuperTokens web-js' `authenticateCredentialWithSignIn()` should support credential-less sign-in (browser shows the picker for any credential registered to the origin). If their API requires an email/userID first, we'd have to fall back to Pattern (B). I'll verify during implementation — if it forces a userID, we revisit this question.

**Pick (A), (B), or (C)?**

> DEVELOPER

A

I have enough to draft the design. The remaining decisions (RP ID, authenticator type policy, re-auth semantics, recovery, rate limiting) are mostly safe defaults that don't change the architecture. I'll bake them in with rationale; you can flag anything you'd rather change.

## Design — Settings → Authentication (passkey enrolment + sign-in)

### Architecture

```
Browser (Vue SPA)
  │
  ├── /settings → "Authentication" tab (NEW)
  │     ├── List passkeys (label, created_at, last_used_at, "current device" badge)
  │     ├── "Add passkey" button → WebAuthn ceremony → Settings refresh
  │     └── "Remove" → confirm dialog → delete credential
  │
  ├── /login → existing Google button + NEW "Sign in with Passkey" button
  │
  └── supertokens-web-js v0.16.0  (Session + ThirdParty + NEW Webauthn recipe)
        │
        │ /auth/webauthn/*
        ▼
Go API (existing SuperTokensMiddleware proxy)
        │
        ▼
SuperTokens core (Postgres-backed)  ← owns credential storage
        │
        ▼ post-signIn hook
Raven users table  ← syncs external_id ↔ users.id (same pattern as Google ThirdParty)
```

### Decisions locked from grilling

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Both enrolment + sign-in shipped together | User asked for both; splitting ships invisible value |
| Q2 | SuperTokens Webauthn recipe (web-js side; Go SDK doesn't have it but middleware proxies) | Single source of truth; matches Google ThirdParty pattern |
| Q3 | Multiple passkeys per user, user-labeled, capped at 10 | Real users have multi-device; labels enable safe revocation |
| Q4 | Login page: 2 buttons (Google + Passkey), no email-first | Minimal change; passkeys are origin-scoped |

### Safe defaults baked in (flag any you'd change)

- **RP ID = `ravencloak.org`** (covers all subdomains). Passkeys enrolled on `demo.ravencloak.org` will work on `app.ravencloak.org` later. If you'd rather keep them isolated, switch to per-subdomain RP IDs.
- **Authenticator policy = any.** Platform (Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello) AND cross-platform (YubiKey, USB security keys) both accepted. `userVerification: "required"` (biometric/PIN at credential use — no touch-only).
- **Re-auth for credential changes:** The WebAuthn add ceremony itself requires biometric/PIN, so adding is implicitly re-authed. Removal uses a confirm dialog only (matches GitHub's pattern for SSH key removal). No separate "sudo mode" in v1.
- **Recovery:** Google sign-in is always available as fallback. If you lose all passkeys, sign in via Google then enrol new ones. (No special recovery codes in v1; SuperTokens' MFA recipe can add them later.)
- **Rate limiting:** SuperTokens core handles ceremony rate-limiting natively. We don't add anything Raven-side.
- **Default label** at enrolment time pre-fills from `navigator.userAgent` parsing (e.g. "MacBook · Chrome 142"). User can override before saving.
- **Cap = 10 passkeys per user.** Sanity guard, not friction (median user has ≤ 3).

### What gets built

**Frontend** (`frontend/src/`)
1. `plugins/supertokens.ts` — add `import Webauthn from 'supertokens-web-js/recipe/webauthn'` and `Webauthn.init()` next to existing Session + ThirdParty.
2. `api/passkeys.ts` (NEW) — thin wrapper over `Webauthn.*` methods + a Raven `GET /api/v1/me/passkeys`, `PATCH /api/v1/me/passkeys/:id` (relabel), `DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/:id` for label storage (SuperTokens core doesn't store labels; we keep them in our `users_passkey_labels` table keyed by SuperTokens credential ID).
3. `stores/passkeys.ts` (NEW) — Pinia store: list, add, remove, relabel.
4. `pages/settings/SettingsPage.vue` — new "Authentication" tab + section. List + Add + Remove + Relabel.
5. `pages/LoginPage.vue` — new "Sign in with Passkey" button next to Google. Calls `Webauthn.authenticateCredentialWithSignIn()`.
6. Vitest specs for the store + new tab.

**Backend** (`internal/`)
1. `handler/passkey.go` (NEW) — `GET /api/v1/me/passkeys` (list from SuperTokens core + join our label table), `PATCH .../:id` (update label), `DELETE .../:id` (delete from SuperTokens core via REST + our row). Per spec/ADR-style: org-scoped via existing auth middleware; user-scoped to the caller (NOT org-wide).
2. `handler/auth.go` — extend the existing post-signin user-mapping path to handle the new `webauthn` recipe payload (mirrors the Google ThirdParty path at line 86).
3. `migrations/00054_user_passkey_labels.sql` — single small table `(user_id uuid, credential_id text PRIMARY KEY, label text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz, last_used_at timestamptz NULL)`. RLS by user_id.
4. Tests for the handlers (mock SuperTokens core HTTP).

**Infra**
1. Verify deployed SuperTokens core image exposes `/auth/webauthn/*`. If `:latest` doesn't, pin to a known-good version in `docker-compose.yml`.

**Docs**
1. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-04-passkey-auth-design.md` (this spec — to write)
2. CONTEXT.md glossary additions: **Passkey**, **Authenticator**, **WebAuthn**.

### Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Conditional-UI auto-prompt on login page (Q4 option C).
- Email-first sign-in flow (Q4 option B).
- "Sudo mode" / time-bound re-auth window for credential changes.
- Recovery codes.
- Cross-subdomain UX for credential management.

---

**This is the design proposal.** Looks right? Flag any default you want different (RP ID scope, authenticator policy, label cap, etc.) and I'll revise before writing the spec file.

  "content": "# M14 — Passkey Authentication (WebAuthn)\n\n**Status:** Draft (review pending)\n**Date:** 2026-06-04\n**Milestone:** M14 — Passkey Authentication\n\n## Problem\n\nRaven's only sign-in method today is Google ThirdParty via SuperTokens. This forces every user through a Google account, which:\n\n- Excludes users without a Google identity (or who refuse to use one for this product).\n- Adds an external dependency on Google availability and OAuth-consent UX for every sign-in.\n- Doesn't allow a user to bind their account to a strong hardware credential (phishing-resistant).\n\nPasskeys (WebAuthn) solve all three: they are phishing-resistant by construction, work without an external identity provider, and run inside the user's own authenticator (Touch ID, Windows Hello, security key).\n\n## Goals\n\n1. A logged-in user can enrol one or more passkeys for the current device via **Settings → Authentication**.\n2. A user with an enrolled passkey can sign in by clicking **\"Sign in with Passkey\"** on the login page — no email entry, browser picks any matching credential for the origin.\n3. Google ThirdParty sign-in continues to work unchanged; passkey is purely additive.\n4. Lost-device recovery is implicit: sign in with Google, then re-enrol new passkeys.\n5. Credentials are stored by SuperTokens core (single source of truth for auth artifacts, matching the Google ThirdParty pattern).\n\n## Non-Goals (v1)\n\n- \"Sudo mode\" / time-bound re-auth before credential changes. The WebAuthn add ceremony itself requires biometric/PIN.\n- Recovery codes — SuperTokens MFA recipe can add these later.\n- Conditional-UI auto-prompt on login page (Q4 option C in brainstorming).\n- Email-first sign-in flow (Q4 option B).\n- Email/password sign-up — passkey replaces the need for one.\n- Cross-tenant credential sharing or any per-Org passkey concepts; passkeys are per-User.\n\n## Decisions (grilled, all locked)\n\n| # | Question | Decision | Reason |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Q1 | Scope | Enrolment **and** sign-in shipped together | User asked for both; splitting ships invisible value |\n| Q2 | Implementation | SuperTokens **Webauthn recipe** via `supertokens-web-js@0.16.0`; Go SDK has no webauthn recipe but existing `SuperTokensMiddleware` proxies `/auth/webauthn/*` to the core | One source of truth; matches Google ThirdParty pattern; no new auth state outside SuperTokens |\n| Q3 | Multi-passkey | Multiple, user-labeled, capped at 10 per user | Real users have multi-device; labels enable safe revocation |\n| Q4 | Login UX | Two buttons (Google + Passkey) on login page, no email-first | Minimal page change; passkeys are origin-scoped so no email lookup needed |\n\n## Safe defaults (flagged in design review, can revise)\n\n- **RP ID:** `ravencloak.org` (covers all subdomains so a passkey enrolled on `demo.ravencloak.org` works on `app.ravencloak.org` too).\n- **Authenticator types:** any — platform (Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello) and cross-platform (YubiKey, USB security keys) both accepted. `userVerification: \"required\"`.\n- **Re-auth for changes:** the WebAuthn add ceremony's biometric/PIN is treated as implicit re-auth. Removal uses a confirm dialog (matches GitHub SSH-key UX).\n- **Recovery:** Google sign-in is always the fallback. No recovery codes in v1.\n- **Rate limiting:** SuperTokens core handles ceremony rate-limiting natively.\n- **Default label** pre-fills from `navigator.userAgent` parsing (\"MacBook · Chrome 142\"); user can override.\n- **Cap:** 10 passkeys per user — sanity guard, median user has ≤ 3.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```text\n                              Vue 3 SPA (supertokens-web-js 0.16.0)\n                                          │\n                  ┌───────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐\n                  │                       │                         │\n        Settings → Authentication      Login page             plugins/supertokens.ts\n        (NEW tab)                      (NEW button)           Session + ThirdParty + NEW Webauthn\n                  │                       │                         │\n                  ▼                       ▼                         │\n        stores/passkeys.ts (Pinia)   Webauthn.authenticate          │\n        list, add, remove, relabel   CredentialWithSignIn()         │\n                  │                       │                         │\n                  └───────┬───────────────┘                         │\n                          │                                         │\n                          ▼                                         │\n              api/passkeys.ts (Raven)         /auth/webauthn/* ◄────┘\n              GET    /api/v1/me/passkeys      (proxied by existing\n              PATCH  /api/v1/me/passkeys/:id   SuperTokensMiddleware)\n              DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/:id            │\n                          │                             ▼\n                          ▼                  SuperTokens core (Postgres)\n              Go: internal/handler/passkey.go   ← credential storage\n                          │                             │\n                          ▼                             │ post-signIn hook\n              Raven users + new user_passkey_labels ◄───┘\n              (label/created_at/last_used_at,           (syncs external_id ↔ users.id,\n               keyed on SuperTokens credential ID;       same pattern as Google ThirdParty)\n               RLS by user_id)\n```\n\n## Data flow\n\n### Enrolment (Settings → Authentication → Add passkey)\n\n1. User clicks **Add passkey**. Frontend pre-fills label from `navigator.userAgent`.\n2. Frontend calls `Webauthn.getRegisterOptions()` → proxied to `/auth/webauthn/options/register` on core → returns challenge.\n3. Frontend calls `Webauthn.createCredential(options)` → browser opens authenticator (biometric/PIN) → returns credential.\n4. Frontend calls `Webauthn.registerCredential(response)` → proxied to `/auth/webauthn/register` on core → core persists credential against current user's SuperTokens ID.\n5. Frontend calls Raven `PATCH /api/v1/me/passkeys/:credentialId { label }` → upserts row in `user_passkey_labels`.\n6. Settings refreshes the list.\n\n### Sign-in (Login page → Sign in with Passkey)\n\n1. User clicks **Sign in with Passkey**. No email input.\n2. Frontend calls `Webauthn.authenticateCredentialWithSignIn()` → browser picker (all matching credentials for `ravencloak.org`) → user picks one, completes biometric.\n3. Frontend's response includes the SuperTokens session tokens. Raven's existing post-signin hook fires, mapping the SuperTokens user ID to `users.id`.\n4. Redirect to dashboard.\n\n### Removal (Settings → Authentication → Remove)\n\n1. User clicks **Remove** on a passkey row → confirm dialog.\n2. Frontend calls Raven `DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/:credentialId` → handler:\n   - Authn check: caller must own this credential (verify via SuperTokens core lookup).\n   - Calls SuperTokens core REST `DELETE /recipe/webauthn/user/credential` → core removes credential.\n   - Deletes our `user_passkey_labels` row.\n3. Settings refreshes.\n\n## Components\n\n### Frontend (`frontend/src/`)\n\n| File | Change |\n|---|---|\n| `plugins/supertokens.ts` | Add `import Webauthn from 'supertokens-web-js/recipe/webauthn'` + `Webauthn.init()` next to Session and ThirdParty. |\n| `api/passkeys.ts` (NEW) | Thin wrapper: `listPasskeys`, `relabelPasskey`, `removePasskey`. Uses existing `authFetch`. |\n| `stores/passkeys.ts` (NEW) | Pinia store: `passkeys`, `fetchPasskeys`, `addPasskey`, `removePasskey`, `relabelPasskey`. Optimistic UI with rollback. |\n| `pages/settings/SettingsPage.vue` | Add new `Authentication` tab + section. List with label/created/last-used columns; Add and Remove actions. |\n| `pages/LoginPage.vue` | Add \"Sign in with Passkey\" button beside the Google button. Calls `Webauthn.authenticateCredentialWithSignIn()`. |\n| `stores/passkeys.spec.ts` (NEW) | Vitest covering list, add (mock Webauthn), remove, relabel, rollback. |\n\n### Backend (`internal/`)\n\n| File | Change |\n|---|---|\n| `handler/passkey.go` (NEW) | `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys[/:id]`. List joins SuperTokens core (HTTP) with `user_passkey_labels`. PATCH upserts label. DELETE calls core's REST + removes our row. User-scoped via session middleware; verify caller owns each credential. |\n| `handler/auth.go` | Extend the post-signin user-mapping path so the existing Google flow is mirrored when the recipe is `webauthn`. Same `external_id` mapping. |\n| `migrations/00054_user_passkey_labels.sql` (NEW) | `(user_id uuid NOT NULL, credential_id text PRIMARY KEY, label text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_used_at timestamptz NULL)`. RLS by user_id. Goose no-transaction; concurrent index on user_id. |\n| `service/passkey.go` (NEW) | Small service wrapping SuperTokens core REST calls (list credentials by user ID, delete credential). |\n| `handler/passkey_test.go` (NEW) | Handler tests with mocked SuperTokens core HTTP. |\n\n### Infra\n\n| File | Change |\n|---|---|\n| `docker-compose.yml` | Pin `registry.supertokens.io/supertokens/supertokens-postgresql` to a version that ships WebAuthn (verify which CDI version first). Add `RAVEN_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=ravencloak.org` and `RAVEN_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=Raven` env vars; backend reads them and forwards to SuperTokens recipe config. |\n| `.env.example` | Document the two new env vars. |\n\n### Docs\n\n- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-04-passkey-auth-design.md` (this file).\n- CONTEXT.md glossary additions (when the parallel Marketplace docs land — for now, defer): **Passkey**, **WebAuthn**, **Authenticator**, **Relying Party (RP)**.\n\n## Out-of-scope follow-ups\n\n- Conditional-UI auto-prompt on login.\n- Email-first sign-in.\n- Sudo-mode / time-bound re-auth before sensitive changes.\n- Recovery codes.\n- Disabling Google sign-in entirely (passkey-only mode).\n\n## Issue breakdown (tracer-bullet vertical slices)\n\nSix issues. **A, B, E are independent and can be implemented in parallel.** C depends on B; D depends on B; F depends on all.\n\n### A — Backend: passkey handler + label migration + service\n\n- New migration `00054_user_passkey_labels.sql` (per Architecture section).\n- New `internal/handler/passkey.go` + `internal/service/passkey.go`.\n- Wire routes into `cmd/api/main.go` under existing auth middleware (user-scoped).\n- Handler tests with mocked SuperTokens core HTTP.\n- Extend `internal/handler/auth.go` post-signin mapping for `webauthn` recipe.\n- Acceptance: GET returns merged credentials+labels; PATCH upserts label; DELETE removes from core + our row; tests pass; lint passes.\n\n### B — Frontend foundation: Webauthn.init + store + api wrapper\n\n- Add `Webauthn.init()` to `plugins/supertokens.ts`.\n- New `api/passkeys.ts` thin wrapper (depends on A for endpoint URLs but URL contract is fixed in this spec).\n- New `stores/passkeys.ts` Pinia store with optimistic updates + rollback.\n- Vitest unit tests for the store.\n- Acceptance: store mocks pass; `Webauthn.init` resolves; lint passes.\n\n### C — Frontend: Settings → Authentication tab\n\n- Add new \"Authentication\" tab to `pages/settings/SettingsPage.vue`.\n- Section: list of passkeys (label, created_at, last_used_at, \"current device\" badge), Add button, Remove button per row, inline relabel.\n- Default label from UA parsing.\n- Empty state: \"No passkeys yet. Add one to skip Google sign-in next time.\"\n- Toast errors on add/remove failure.\n- Depends on Issue B.\n\n### D — Frontend: Login page \"Sign in with Passkey\" button\n\n- Add button beside the existing Google button in `pages/LoginPage.vue`.\n- On click: `Webauthn.authenticateCredentialWithSignIn()`, handle success → redirect; handle `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR` / `WEBAUTHN_NOT_SUPPORTED` with inline error.\n- Disabled state with tooltip if `doesBrowserSupportWebAuthn()` returns false.\n- Depends on Issue B.\n\n### E — Infra: pin SuperTokens core image + RP config env vars\n\n- Probe the current `:latest` SuperTokens core image for WebAuthn endpoint support. If absent, pin to a known-good version in `docker-compose.yml`.\n- Add `RAVEN_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` and `RAVEN_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME` to `.env.example` and to the API container's env.\n- Document in a README or runbook entry.\n- Independent of A/B/C/D.\n\n### F — E2E Playwright coverage\n\n- **Add passkey** — sign in (Google), navigate to Settings → Authentication, click Add, mock the Webauthn ceremony, assert list shows the new entry with the auto-generated label.\n- **Relabel** — click label, type new value, blur, reload, assert persisted.\n- **Remove** — click Remove, confirm, assert row gone.\n- **Sign in with Passkey** — log out, on login page click \"Sign in with Passkey\", mock browser picker, land on dashboard.\n- **Browser unsupported** — mock `doesBrowserSupportWebAuthn` returning false; assert button disabled with tooltip.\n- Depends on A, B, C, D.\n\n## Success criteria\n\n- Logged-in user can add a passkey from Settings → Authentication on first try with no manual config; the ceremony triggers the OS biometric prompt.\n- The new passkey appears in the list with the auto-generated label and \"current device\" badge.\n- Logged out, the user can sign in with a single click + biometric on the login page.\n- Removing a passkey from Settings causes it to no longer work for sign-in (verified by E2E).\n- Google sign-in continues to work exactly as before.\n- Migration `00054` applies cleanly on a fresh DB and a populated one.\n- All existing tests still pass; new tests added per spec.\n- Frontend lint + `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=origin/main` pass.\n- New Playwright scenarios pass headless in CI.\n"

```
src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue(599,5): error TS2322: 
Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'.
```

The exact code:

```ts
createTestStatus.value = result.ok ? 'pass' : 'fail'
createTestDetail.value = result.detail   // ← line 599; result.detail is string | undefined
```

`createTestDetail` is typed `ref<string>` but `TestConnectionResult.detail` is optional (`string | undefined`). One-liner fix: `result.detail ?? ''`.

This is **not** something the M14 PRs introduced — recent file history shows it was probably present since #689 (Test-Connection gate) or #768 (health-check cron). The Build step has been failing for a while; M14 just happened to be the next thing through.

## (2) Why the PRs merged anyway — branch-protection misconfiguration

```
$ gh api repos/ravencloak-org/Raven/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks
{ "contexts": ["Gate", "DCO Sign-off", "Gitleaks"], "strict": false }
```

**The "Build & Deploy" workflow is NOT in the required-checks list.** Auto-merge correctly waits for the 3 required contexts (Gate, DCO Sign-off, Gitleaks — all fast and all passed for the M14 PRs) and ignores the failing optional Build check.

All 6 M14 PRs (777, 778, 779, 780, 781, 782) are merged. Main is broken from a deploy standpoint until the TS error is fixed.

## Recommended fix — two actions

1. **Immediate hotfix:** small PR changing line 599 to `createTestDetail.value = result.detail ?? ''`. Unblocks the Cloudflare Pages deploy.
2. **Process fix:** add the Build & Deploy job context (and likely the Go tests/lint) to the required-checks list on `main` so auto-merge can't fire on a broken build again. Branch-protection edit, no code change.

Want me to spawn both in parallel — a hotfix PR for the TS error and a settings PR / `gh api` call to add the missing required checks?

## Surprises uncovered along the way

1. **B wasn't a quic-go bug at all** — that Dependabot bump was a coincidence. The real cause was the M14 backend's migration #00054 having a `--` comment that *mentioned* `+goose NO TRANSACTION` in prose. Goose's parser treats `--+goose` as an annotation regardless of context, broke `goose.Up` across 5 packages, masked as the test failure that looked like the quic-go bump.
2. **C is also an M14 self-inflicted wound** — the E2E spec (PR #782) and the Settings UI (PR #780) were written in parallel from the same spec doc but landed with diverging testid names (`add-passkey-btn` vs `passkey-add-button`). Plus a deeper config issue: `playwright.config.ts` sets `testIdAttribute: 'data-test'`, but the codebase mostly uses `data-testid` — every test that tried to use `getByTestId` was working against a different attribute. Issue #787 owns the proper fix.

Once these four PRs land, all four red workflows go green again and the branch-protection update means we won't be able to merge through a broken build like this happened.

-- Passkey labels (issue #771, M14).

-- Stores user-supplied labels and timestamps for WebAuthn credentials managed
-- by the SuperTokens core. The core itself owns the credential (public key,
-- attestation, counter, transports); Raven only stores the human-readable
-- label and the last-used timestamp so the Settings → Authentication tab can
-- render meaningful rows like "MacBook Pro Touch ID" instead of opaque IDs.
--
-- credential_id is the SuperTokens credential identifier and is the natural
-- primary key — there is exactly one label row per credential. user_id is
-- duplicated here (rather than joining via the core) so RLS can scope reads
-- by tenant without a cross-service round trip on every request.
--
-- Concurrent index on user_id supports the GET /api/v1/me/passkeys query
-- (which lists every label for the calling user in one shot). Built
-- CONCURRENTLY so the deploy does not hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table
-- while the index is built — this is why the migration is wrapped in the
-- goose "NO TRANSACTION" annotation above (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
-- cannot run inside a transaction block).
--
-- References:
--   - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-04-passkey-auth-design.md §Architecture
--   - migrations/00015_rls_policies.sql (tenant_isolation + admin_bypass)
--   - migrations/00004_users.sql (users.id FK target, UUID PK)

-- Bound the locks taken by the DDL below so a long-running query cannot
-- block production indefinitely. The CREATE TABLE + ADD CONSTRAINT take
-- ACCESS EXCLUSIVE briefly; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY takes a weaker lock
-- but a generous statement_timeout protects against runaway builds on a
-- large users table.
SET lock_timeout = '5s';
SET statement_timeout = '30s';

CREATE TABLE user_passkey_labels (
    user_id       UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    credential_id TEXT        PRIMARY KEY,
    label         TEXT        NOT NULL CHECK (length(label) BETWEEN 1 AND 255),
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_used_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NULL
);

-- Enable RLS so a stray query without app.current_user_id set sees zero
-- rows by default. Pattern mirrors migrations/00015 + the per-user variant
-- used by marketplace_reports (00053_marketplace_moderation.sql).
ALTER TABLE user_passkey_labels ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Self-read/write: callers see only rows whose user_id matches the session

// ownsCredential confirms the caller actually owns the credential by
// listing the core's credentials for the session user and checking

// a 403 (or 500 on lookup failure) and returns false.
//
// This is the authorisation backstop: the routes already sit under the
// session middleware, but PATCH/DELETE accept the credential ID as a URL
// parameter and we must not trust it.
func (h *PasskeyHandler) ownsCredential(c *gin.Context, externalID, credentialID string) bool {
	creds, err := h.svc.ListByUser(c.Request.Context(), externalID)
	if err != nil {
		_ = c.Error(apierror.NewInternal("passkey ownership check failed: " + err.Error()))
		c.Abort()
		return false

	for _, cred := range creds {

	_ = c.Error(&apierror.AppError{
		Code:    http.StatusForbidden,
		Message: "Forbidden",
		Detail:  "credential does not belong to caller",
	})
	c.Abort()
	return false
}

# passkey handler implementation

// Package handler — passkey.go is the HTTP layer for the passkey
// management endpoints under /api/v1/me/passkeys. All routes assume the
// session middleware has populated ContextKeyUserID + ContextKeyExternalID
// (i.e. they sit under the standard authenticated /api/v1 group).
package handler

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/db"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/middleware"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/internal/service"
	"github.com/ravencloak-org/Raven/pkg/apierror"
)

// PasskeyServicer is the subset of *service.PasskeyService the handler
// needs. Defined as an interface so handler tests can inject a stub
// without touching the live SuperTokens core.
type PasskeyServicer interface {
	ListByUser(ctx context.Context, externalUserID string) ([]service.PasskeyCredential, error)
	DeleteCredential(ctx context.Context, externalUserID, credentialID string) error
}

// PasskeyLabelStore is the subset of *pgxpool.Pool the handler exercises.
// Allowing nil + a labelStoreOverride field on the handler keeps tests free
// of the pool entirely — they can simulate the DB by injecting a fake.
type PasskeyLabelStore interface {
	ListLabelsForUser(ctx context.Context, userID string) (map[string]passkeyLabelRow, error)
	UpsertLabel(ctx context.Context, userID, credentialID, label string) error
	DeleteLabel(ctx context.Context, userID, credentialID string) error
}

// passkeyLabelRow is the projected shape we need from
// user_passkey_labels for the GET join.
type passkeyLabelRow struct {
	Label      string
	CreatedAt  time.Time
	LastUsedAt *time.Time
}

// PasskeyHandler wires the SuperTokens core (via PasskeyServicer) to the
// local user_passkey_labels table.
type PasskeyHandler struct {
	svc   PasskeyServicer
	store PasskeyLabelStore
}

// NewPasskeyHandler constructs a handler backed by the supplied service and
// a real pgxpool-backed label store. Tests construct the handler with
// NewPasskeyHandlerWithStore so they can substitute a fake store.
func NewPasskeyHandler(svc PasskeyServicer, pool *pgxpool.Pool) *PasskeyHandler {
	return &PasskeyHandler{svc: svc, store: &pgxPasskeyLabelStore{pool: pool}}
}

// NewPasskeyHandlerWithStore is the test seam — pass a fake PasskeyLabelStore
// and the handler will route every DB call through it.
func NewPasskeyHandlerWithStore(svc PasskeyServicer, store PasskeyLabelStore) *PasskeyHandler {
	return &PasskeyHandler{svc: svc, store: store}
}

// passkeyResponseItem is one row in the merged GET response.
type passkeyResponseItem struct {
	CredentialID string     `json:"credential_id"`
	Label        string     `json:"label"`
	CreatedAt    time.Time  `json:"created_at"`
	LastUsedAt   *time.Time `json:"last_used_at,omitempty"`
}

// passkeyPatchRequest is the body of PATCH /api/v1/me/passkeys/:credential_id.

### passkey handler implementation (3)
// requireSession pulls both the internal user ID and the SuperTokens
// external ID off the request context. Both are required: external for
// the core API, internal for the label table.
func (h *PasskeyHandler) requireSession(c *gin.Context) (userID, externalID string, ok bool) {
	userIDVal, _ := c.Get(string(middleware.ContextKeyUserID))
	uid, _ := userIDVal.(string)
	extVal, _ := c.Get(string(middleware.ContextKeyExternalID))
	ext, _ := extVal.(string)
	if uid == "" || ext == "" {
		_ = c.Error(apierror.NewUnauthorized("missing user identity"))
		c.Abort()
		return "", "", false
	}
	return uid, ext, true
}

// ownsCredential confirms the caller actually owns the credential by
// listing the core's credentials for the session user and checking
// membership. Returns true when ownership is confirmed; otherwise writes
// a 403 (or 500 on lookup failure) and returns false.
//
// This is the authorisation backstop: the routes already sit under the
// session middleware, but PATCH/DELETE accept the credential ID as a URL
// parameter and we must not trust it.
func (h *PasskeyHandler) ownsCredential(c *gin.Context, externalID, credentialID string) bool {
	creds, err := h.svc.ListByUser(c.Request.Context(), externalID)
	if err != nil {
		_ = c.Error(apierror.NewInternal("passkey ownership check failed: " + err.Error()))
		c.Abort()
		return false
	}
	for _, cred := range creds {
		if cred.CredentialID == credentialID {
			return true
		}
	}
	_ = c.Error(&apierror.AppError{
		Code:    http.StatusForbidden,
		Message: "Forbidden",
		Detail:  "credential does not belong to caller",
	})
	c.Abort()
	return false
}

// pgxPasskeyLabelStore implements PasskeyLabelStore against the live
// user_passkey_labels table. RLS is enforced by setting
// app.current_user_id inside the wrapping transaction (db.WithUserID).
type pgxPasskeyLabelStore struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

// ListLabelsForUser returns label rows keyed by credential_id.
func (s *pgxPasskeyLabelStore) ListLabelsForUser(ctx context.Context, userID string) (map[string]passkeyLabelRow, error) {
	out := make(map[string]passkeyLabelRow)
	err := db.WithUserID(ctx, s.pool, userID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		rows, err := tx.Query(ctx,
			`SELECT credential_id, label, created_at, last_used_at
			 FROM user_passkey_labels
			 WHERE user_id = $1`, userID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		defer rows.Close()
		for rows.Next() {
			var (
				credID     string
				row        passkeyLabelRow
				lastUsedAt *time.Time
			)
			if err := rows.Scan(&credID, &row.Label, &row.CreatedAt, &lastUsedAt); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			row.LastUsedAt = lastUsedAt
			out[credID] = row
		}
		return rows.Err()
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

  async function removePasskey(credentialId: string): Promise<void> {
    error.value = null
    const snapshot = passkeys.value.slice()
    passkeys.value = passkeys.value.filter(
      (p) => p.credential_id !== credentialId,
    )
    try {
      await removePasskeyApi(credentialId)
    } catch (e) {
      passkeys.value = snapshot
      error.value = (e as Error).message
      throw e
    }
  }

  async function relabelPasskey(
    credentialId: string,
    label: string,
  ): Promise<void> {
    error.value = null
    const snapshot = passkeys.value.slice()
    const idx = findIndex(passkeys.value, (p) => p.credential_id === credentialId)
    if (idx === -1) {
      // Nothing to update — surface a no-op error so the caller can
      // refetch instead of silently ignoring the request.
      throw new Error(`Passkey ${credentialId} not found in local state`)
    }
    passkeys.value[idx] = { ...passkeys.value[idx], label }
    try {
      const updated = await relabelPasskeyApi(credentialId, label)
      passkeys.value[idx] = updated
    } catch (e) {
      passkeys.value = snapshot
      error.value = (e as Error).message
      throw e
    }
  }

    passkeys,
    loading,
    error,
    fetchPasskeys,
    addPasskey,
    removePasskey,
    relabelPasskey,
  }

1212 +615  (PR #689 rebase: Test-Connection dialog + tunnel hints + install hints + ungrounded fallback wiring)
```

5.7× growth in one month. **No single PR is responsible** — each landed below the 1k-line line, and the size compounds. The file now contains:

- Create dialog (provider type, model, base URL, API key, install hints)
- Edit-credentials dialog (rotate-key disclosure, test re-gate)
- Card rendering (default pill, make-default, inline rename + model swap)
- **Two copies** of the test-connection state machine (`createTestStatus` / `editTestStatus`)
- Tunnel hint UI (Cloudflare + ngrok one-liners + clipboard)
- Default-switch toast + confirm-delete dialog

The agent who landed #689 had to rename `testStatus` → `createTestStatus` to avoid colliding with the Edit dialog's `editTestStatus`. **That collision is the codebase telling you to extract a composable.**

### Code-judo: decompose

```
LlmProviderListPage.vue        (top-level orchestration + list rendering)
├── ProviderCard.vue            (inline edits + actions + default pill)
├── CreateProviderDialog.vue    (form + Test gate)
├── EditCredentialsDialog.vue   (rotate-key + Test re-gate)
├── TunnelHint.vue              (reusable Ollama-loopback hint block)
└── composables/useTestConnectionGate.ts   (idle|testing|pass|fail + invalidate-on-change)
```

`useTestConnectionGate` is the highest-impact extraction: it deletes duplication between the two dialogs and removes the naming collision the rename papered over.

This was supposed to be M13's win — the spec promised a "unified responsive card" but didn't promise the page would also absorb every dialog. It accreted.

---

## 🚨 Presumptive blocker 2 — `cmd/api/main.go` is 1127 lines

Was ~1045 pre-M14; M14 added 82. The file holds every route registration inline. The recently-deployed **duplicate `/llm-providers/test` route registration** (the bug that crashed the demo until we patched it out) was a direct consequence of this shape: when all routes are in one 1k-line function, you can't see them at once and duplicates land.

### Code-judo: extract route-wiring helpers

One helper per resource group:

```go
// cmd/api/wire_routes.go
func wirePasskeyRoutes(api *gin.RouterGroup, h *handler.PasskeyHandler) {
    api.GET("/me/passkeys", h.List)
    api.PATCH("/me/passkeys/:credential_id", h.Patch)
    api.DELETE("/me/passkeys/:credential_id", h.Delete)
}
```

main() shrinks to construction + a sequence of `wireX` calls. Duplicate routes become impossible at the call site (compiler / linter complains).

Start the pattern with the M14 passkey block; migrate the rest as new features land.

---

## Code-judo misses

### 1. `pgxPasskeyLabelStore` is in `internal/handler/passkey.go`. It belongs in `internal/repository/`.

The codebase has `ChunkRepository`, `DocumentRepository`, `LLMProviderRepository`. SQL in a handler file is an architecture-boundary leak, makes the handler file harder to scan, and breaks the layering convention. Move to `internal/repository/passkey_label.go`. The handler then holds only HTTP concerns.

### 2. Two interfaces + two constructors for one handler is over-engineered

```go
type PasskeyServicer interface { … }      // 2 methods
type PasskeyLabelStore interface { … }    // 3 methods
func NewPasskeyHandler(svc, pool)         // production
func NewPasskeyHandlerWithStore(svc, store) // test seam
```

That's 4 concepts for what's structurally one struct + an injected service. Collapse to a single `PasskeyService` interface (5 methods) and one constructor; tests wire a mock service. Matches how `ChatService` and the other Go services in this repo are tested.

### 3. `ownsCredential` doubles the wire traffic on every PATCH/DELETE

```go
func (h *PasskeyHandler) ownsCredential(...) bool {
    creds, err := h.svc.ListByUser(ctx, externalID)  // ← full HTTP round-trip to SuperTokens core
    // linear search through creds
}
```

Every label edit hits the core to list **all** the user's credentials just to membership-check one ID. Defense-in-depth is fine but this is the wrong layer:

- **PATCH (label-only):** `UPDATE user_passkey_labels SET label=$1 WHERE credential_id=$2 AND user_id=$3` — row-count tells you ownership atomically, zero core calls.
- **DELETE:** trust the core's own ownership check on its DELETE endpoint; map "not found" → 404. No pre-check needed.

This isn't a perf nit — it's two wire calls where one belongs.

### 4. `db.WithUserID` is a near-copy of `db.WithOrgID`

```go
func WithUserID(ctx, pool, userID, fn) error {
    tx, err := pool.Begin(ctx)
    defer tx.Rollback(ctx)
    if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, "SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)", userID); ...
    if err := fn(tx); ...
    return tx.Commit(ctx)
}
```

Same shape as `WithOrgID` with a different variable name. Today: 2 copies of this scaffolding. The third caller (workspace? Tenant? Membership?) will copy a third. Extract:

```go
func withRLSVar(ctx, pool, varName, varValue, fn) error { … }
func WithOrgID(ctx, pool, orgID, fn) error  { return withRLSVar(ctx, pool, "app.current_org_id", orgID, fn) }
func WithUserID(ctx, pool, userID, fn) error { return withRLSVar(ctx, pool, "app.current_user_id", userID, fn) }
```

20 lines deleted, contract unchanged.

### 5. `addPasskey` split-state risk

If the Webauthn ceremony succeeds (credential lands in SuperTokens core) but the subsequent label `PATCH` fails (network, timeout, etc.), the credential is registered with no Raven-side label. Next page render shows a credential with `label: ""` — orphan that the user can't easily identify before revoking.

Two clean fixes (better is (b)):

- **(a)** Catch the PATCH failure → compensating DELETE on the core. Doubles failure modes.
- **(b)** Move label creation into the existing **post-signin hook** at `internal/handler/auth.go:86` that already maps SuperTokens user IDs to local `users.id` rows. The hook fires on every successful credential registration; label gets persisted in the same transaction that records the user. Zero client-side error path needed.

---

## Smaller findings

- **PasskeysSection.vue at `pages/settings/`** is fine but inconsistent with how other compound sections in the codebase live under `components/`. Move to `components/settings/PasskeysSection.vue` to match.
- **Spec promised** RP_ID/RP_NAME env vars would flow to the SuperTokens recipe init. PR #781 noted in its body they're "currently informational" because the Go SDK has no webauthn recipe. That's accurate but means we have unused config that future devs will assume works. Either delete the env vars until they're wired, or wire them via a tenant-init REST call to the core now.

---

## What's good and should stay

- Migration `00054` is exemplary: NO TRANSACTION + CONCURRENTLY + RLS policies + foreign keys + length checks + squawk-ignores added with comments explaining why.
- `PasskeysSection.vue` was extracted as the spec called for; SettingsPage only grew by 5 lines.
- The passkey backend handler's response shapes are well-typed and JSON-tagged consistently.
- The frontend store's optimistic-update + snapshot-rollback pattern is consistent with the M13 LLM-provider store.
- The post-signin user-mapping extension in `auth.go` follows the existing Google ThirdParty pattern — correct layer choice.

---

## Verdict

**Do not approve.** Two blocker conditions trip the skill's bar:

1. `LlmProviderListPage.vue` blew past 1000 lines (without a single PR being to blame, which is the worst kind of file growth — nobody owns the decomposition).
2. `cmd/api/main.go` is past 1000 lines and the recent duplicate-route bug is direct evidence the size is now causing real-world breakage.

**Required for approval (in priority order):**

1. Decompose `LlmProviderListPage.vue` into the 4 files + 1 composable above. The composable (`useTestConnectionGate`) is the load-bearing change — it deletes the `createTestStatus` / `editTestStatus` duplication.
2. Move `pgxPasskeyLabelStore` to `internal/repository/`.
3. Collapse `PasskeyServicer` + `PasskeyLabelStore` interfaces to one, drop one constructor.
4. Replace `ownsCredential`'s pre-check with row-count-based ownership in the SQL (PATCH) and trust-core (DELETE).
5. Extract `withRLSVar` from `WithOrgID` / `WithUserID`.

**Recommended next:**

6. Begin route-wiring extraction in `cmd/api/main.go` starting with `wirePasskeyRoutes`.
7. Move passkey-label creation into the post-signin SuperTokens hook to eliminate the split-state risk in `addPasskey`.

## Architectural Deepening Opportunities – Raven Codebase Scout Report

Based on systematic analysis of the Raven repo, here are the top high-impact architectural friction points, ranked by severity:

### 1. **Provider Router Duplication: Chat vs. Embedding Resolution**
**Where**: `/internal/service/chat.go` (657 lines), `/internal/service/embed_provider_resolver.go` (114 lines), `/internal/repository/llm_provider.go` (197 lines)

**Friction**: Provider routing logic scattered across two places. `chat.go` contains `resolveDefaultProvider()` that mirrors logic in `embed_provider_resolver.go`'s `resolveEmbeddingProviderFrom()`. Both call the same repo to list/get providers, then execute overlapping priority logic. Callers must wire both and understand the contract split across files. 

**Deletion test**: If you deleted `embed_provider_resolver.go`, its 15-line pure decision function and DB-fetch wrapper would scatter into 3+ call sites. The logic itself is load-bearing; the Module is just pulling it into a seam.

**Cross-file understanding required**: handler → chat.go → repo.GetDefault/List → embed_provider_resolver.go → back to repo. Five-file dependency chain for one domain concept (provider selection).

---

### 2. **Shallow Transaction Scope Boilerplate: 141 WithOrgID Calls Across Service Layer**
**Where**: `/internal/db/db.go` (14 lines), `/internal/service/*.go` (141 instances across airbyte, apikey, chat, conversation, kb, llm_provider, etc.)

**Friction**: Every service function must manually wrap repo calls in `db.WithOrgID(ctx, pool, orgID, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {...})`. This is a 3-line callback boilerplate present in every single multi-query operation. The `WithOrgID` module itself is elegant, but the Interface (set RLS scope + begin/commit tx) leaks to every service. No abstraction over transaction lifetime management per org.

**Deletion test**: If you deleted `WithOrgID`, the same 141 lines would re-scatter as manual `Begin/SetConfig/Commit` in service code. The seam is correctly placed, but handlers have to know about it.

**Escalation risk**: Adding a new per-tenant scope (e.g., `WithWorkspaceID`) would require touching all 141 call sites or creating yet another wrapper.

---

### 3. **LlmProviderListPage.vue Monolith: 1212 Lines, 9 Stores, 5+ State Machines**
**Where**: `/frontend/src/pages/llm-providers/LlmProviderListPage.vue` (1212 lines)

**Friction**: Single file owns create-dialog state, edit-dialog state, delete-dialog state, test-result cache, default-switch pending state, error toast state, and model-dropdown mapping. Each dialog is a sub-state machine (form, validation, test status, in-flight flag). Pinia stores (`useLlmProvidersStore`, `useLlmProviderHealthStore`, `useAuthStore`) are read-only wrappers around API calls with no local caching logic to justify the layering.

**Deletion test**: Extracted to 4 files (Create/Edit/Delete dialogs + main list), the page would shrink to 300 lines and each dialog would become unit-testable. Complexity doesn't vanish; it's just bundled.

**Seam issue**: The 5 `ref()` state vars and 3 computed Health/Default signals are inter-dependent (change provider → reset model → clear test status). No single state contract; reader must trace all the wiring.

---

### 4. **Chat Service: 657 Lines with 4 Dependencies + 2 Optional Decorators**
**Where**: `/internal/service/chat.go` (657 lines, 3 constructors, 5 With* methods)

**Friction**: `ChatService` has `NewChatService()`, `NewChatServiceWithDeps()`, then `WithConversationMemory()`, `WithLLMProviderRepo()`, `WithKBStatusGuard()`. Test setup requires manually wiring the right combination. Interface boundary is unclear: is the Contract the full 657-line surface, or just `StreamCompletion()`?

**Deletion test**: The service is not shallow; it orchestrates 3 concerns (conversation memory, provider resolution, KB status). But the construction pattern (2 factories + 3 optional builders) suggests over-parameterization for testability rather than a natural separation of concerns.

**Locality issue**: Provider resolution (`resolveDefaultProvider + ResolveEmbeddingProvider`) is 20% of the file's complexity and lives inside a 400-line `StreamCompletion()` method. Hard to test the provider-fallback logic without mocking a GRPC client.

---

### 5. **Handler Direct Database Access: PasskeyHandler Stores Labels**
**Where**: `/internal/handler/passkey.go` (348 lines), lines 288–342: `pgxPasskeyLabelStore` struct

**Friction**: `PasskeyHandler` constructs its own `pgxPasskeyLabelStore` (wrapping `pgxpool.Pool`) to manage passkey labels. It's the only handler with embedded repository logic. Other handlers delegate to service layer. This creates a two-tier pattern: handlers usually call services, but passkey bypasses that.

**Deletion test**: If you deleted the embedded `pgxPasskeyLabelStore`, labels would scatter into `PasskeyService` (doesn't exist yet) or the repository layer. The handler is taking on persistence logic that could belong in a dedicated service.

**Seam issue**: Future features needing passkey labels (audit log, encryption rotation) would hit the handler directly, not a service abstraction.

---

### 6. **Mega-Service in main.go: 1143 Lines of Route Wiring**
**Where**: `/cmd/api/main.go` (1143 lines), lines 150–1000+: route registration inline

**Friction**: All HTTP routes are wired in `main()` as direct handler constructor calls. No route package, no registry, no separation of route groups. Adding a new endpoint requires editing main.go. With ~30 handlers, visibility is fragmented: you can't see all user-facing routes in one place.

**Deletion test**: If you extracted routes to a separate `routes/` package with a `Register(gin.Engine)` function per domain (chat, kb, voice, etc.), main would shrink and routes become composable. But today, it's a seam-boundary issue: every handler constructor is hardcoded into the bootstrap function.

---

### 7. **Passkey Handler's Dual Interface Design**
**Where**: `/internal/handler/passkey.go`, lines 26–64 (two constructors, two interfaces)

**Friction**: `PasskeyHandler` exports both `NewPasskeyHandler(svc, pool)` and `NewPasskeyHandlerWithStore(svc, store)`. The `store` parameter is a minimal interface (`PasskeyLabelStore`: 2 methods). This suggests the handler was refactored to support testing without Postgres, but the production path still uses the pool-backed store.

**Deletion test**: If you deleted one constructor, the other would still work; they're alternatives, not layering. But having two suggests the interface (PasskeyLabelStore) isn't the true Contract — the real seam is the handler's need for label persistence, which could be satisfied by a service instead.

---

### 8. **Whatsapp Webhook JSON Parsing: 334 Lines, 33 JSON.Unmarshal Calls**
**Where**: `/internal/handler/whatsapp_webhook.go` (334 lines)

**Friction**: Handler directly unmarshals Meta's webhook JSON (~33 call sites). No schema abstraction; parsing logic is tightly coupled to the handler. Adding a new webhook type (e.g., Instagram, TikTok) would duplicate this parsing.

**Deletion test**: Extracted to `internal/webhook/` package with a `Parser` interface and adapters per vendor, handler would shrink to 150 lines. Parsing isn't inherent to HTTP handling; it's a protocol detail.

---

### 9. **Pinia Stores as Thin API Wrappers**
**Where**: `/frontend/src/stores/llm-providers.ts` (light wrapper), `/frontend/src/stores/passkeys.ts` (6021 lines — much heavier), etc.

**Friction**: `llm-providers.ts` is ~150 lines that just call `/api/llm-providers.ts` functions and manage a `providers` ref. No local caching logic, no conflict resolution, no optimistic updates. It's a store for the sake of Pinia pattern compliance, not a seam that adds value.

**Deletion test**: Components could import from `api/llm-providers.ts` directly, manage their own `const providers = ref([])`. The store doesn't reduce complexity; it adds a layer.

---

### 10. **Embed Provider Model Support Hardcoding**
**Where**: `/internal/model/llm_provider.go`, `embed_provider_resolver.go` lines 85–107

**Friction**: `model.EmbeddingProviderPriority` is a slice like `[ollama, openai, cohere]` hardcoded in the model. Adding a new embedding provider (e.g., Gemini) requires editing two files (model + resolver). The priority logic is in the resolver; the list is in the model.

**Deletion test**: The logic is load-bearing; can't delete. But the seam is misplaced: priority belongs in config, not code.

---

### Summary
The deepest architectural friction points are:
1. **Provider routing split across chat + embed modules** (cross-file understanding)
2. **Boilerplate transaction scoping repeated 141 times** (scalability of new scope types)
3. **LLM provider page monolith** (state complexity, missing component boundaries)
4. **Chat service + provider resolver tangled** (locality of provider logic)
5. **Route wiring in main.go** (no single source of endpoint truth)

These aren't quick fixes; they're seams-in-wrong-places and missing module boundaries that will compound as the codebase grows.

Behavior identical; ~20 lines deleted.\n\nBranch off `origin/main`:\n\n```\ngit fetch origin\ngit checkout -b refactor/db-with-rls-var origin/main\n```\n\n## What's there today\n\n```go\nfunc WithOrgID(ctx, pool, orgID, fn) error {\n    tx, err := pool.Begin(ctx); ... defer rollback\n    tx.Exec(\"SELECT set_config('app.current_org_id', $1, true)\", orgID)\n    fn(tx)\n    return tx.Commit(ctx)\n}\nfunc WithUserID(ctx, pool, userID, fn) error {\n    // same shape, different var name\n    tx.Exec(\"SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)\", userID)\n    ...\n}\n```\n\n## Target shape\n\n```go\n// withRLSVar runs fn in a transaction with a single GUC set to scope RLS.\n// Private — callers use WithOrgID / WithUserID.\nfunc withRLSVar(ctx context.Context, pool *pgxpool.Pool, varName, varValue string, fn func(pgx.Tx) error) error {\n    tx, err := pool.Begin(ctx)\n    if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf(\"begin tx: %w\", err) }\n    defer tx.Rollback(ctx) //nolint:errcheck\n    if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, \"SELECT set_config($1, $2, true)\", varName, varValue); err != nil {\n        return fmt.Errorf(\"set %s: %w\", varName, err)\n    }\n    if err := fn(tx); err != nil { return err }\n    return tx.Commit(ctx)\n}\n\nfunc WithOrgID(ctx, pool, orgID, fn) error  { return withRLSVar(ctx, pool, \"app.current_org_id\", orgID, fn) }\nfunc WithUserID(ctx, pool, userID, fn) error { return withRLSVar(ctx, pool, \"app.current_user_id\", userID, fn) }\n```\n\n## Important — verify the parameterised set_config form is safe\n\nOriginally `db.WithOrgID` hardcoded the var name into the SQL literal (`SELECT set_config('app.current_org_id', $1, true)`). The new helper uses BOTH names as parameters (`$1` and `$2`). Postgres' `set_config` accepts parameterised names — verify with a quick test (the existing `internal/db/migrate_test.go` or a fresh one). If for any reason set_config doesn't accept a parameterised first argument, fall back to building the SQL string from a vetted allow-list of var names rather than using string interpolation.\n\n## Workflow rules — non-negotiable\n\n- Branch: `refactor/db-with-rls-var`\n- Sign every commit (`git commit -s`)\n- **NO `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer**\n- **NEVER `--no-verify`**\n- `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=origin/main ./...` passes\n- `go test ./internal/db/... ./internal/...` passes — RLS tests are the critical safety net\n- `gh pr create --title '...' --body '...' --assignee @me`\n- `gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash`\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- `internal/db/db.go` has one `withRLSVar` + two 1-line public wrappers.\n- All existing `WithOrgID` / `WithUserID` callers compile and pass tests unchanged.\n- A test exercises both wrappers to confirm `current_setting('app.current_org_id')` and `current_setting('app.current_user_id')` return the expected values after the call.\n\n## Reporting\n\nReturn ONLY:\n- PR URL\n- Before/after line count of `internal/db/db.go`\n- Confirmation: parameterised set_config works (or note the fallback)"
